This is the most serious 48 hours in cybersecurity history.

"Black October" they're calling it

It seems every *hour* there's a new incident, that in a typical year, would be one of the biggest incidents of the *entire year*

SUMMARY OF THE LAST 48 HOURS:

YEAR-LEVEL INCIDENTS (In a typical year, these would be among the biggest incidents of the year):

1. PHP2Shell: a hole in the software behind ~70% of websites. Governments took sites offline.
2. eMudhra: the master keys that prove websites are real were cracked. One was the number 4.
3. California: data on every public school student since 2023 stolen, including disability status
4. Railway: hackers stole customers' secret keys from a hosting platform used by millions of developers
5. Zeabur: 321,810 accounts breached. The company is shutting down.
6. LiteLLM: an AI tool downloaded 3.4 million times a day was poisoned with a password stealer
7. GitLab: a 10-out-of-10 severity hole in every version since 2014
8. Cairn: criminals used an AI hacking tool to break into 100+ companies
9. Ahold Delhaize: hackers knocked the owner of Food Lion and Stop & Shop offline
10. Onamae: malware planted on up to 26,739 customer servers in Japan

MONTH-LEVEL INCIDENTS (In a typical month, these would be among the biggest incidents):

11. Signal: a bug could leave your mic and camera on after you hang up
12. NGINX: 3 critical holes in software running ~1/3 of websites
13. HTTP/3: a single connection can crash 7 of the 10 web server types tested
14. Plex: hackers breaking into home media servers
15. SafePay ransomware: FBI warns it has hit 600+ critical infrastructure organizations
16. Palo Alto: ransomware gangs breaking in through company firewalls
17. Bullhorn: platform used by 10,000+ companies knocked offline
18. Medi-Cal: 970,000 patients' data stolen
19. WordPress: hackers stole a plugin maker's keys and used them to plant backdoors on websites
20. AOMEI: backup software's update server handed out a backdoor
21. Meta Muse: Meta's AI agent exposed users' personal and business secrets
22. Tor: 333 relays hijacked to steal logins
23. TiDB Cloud: database company's cloud breached

Also serious:

24. State Bank of India: India's biggest bank confirms a data breach
25. OVHcloud: hackers slipped a password stealer into a cloud company's official tool
26. Siemens: a software hole being used to spread malware
27. North Korea: state hackers launch a new attack campaign on South Korea

text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert 🚨

The Fearless Wallet browser extension is malicious, with a threat exposure period spanning nearly 20 months, from February 2025 to October 2026. Affected versions include 3.0.1 and 3.0.3–3.0.5, containing malicious code designed to steal wallet recovery phrases, private keys, and keystore files when users unlock their wallets.

The stolen data is encrypted using an empty password and exfiltrated through HTTP GET requests to https://t.co/QnsMdsvZzL. A remote configuration file allows attackers to enable or disable the malicious behavior. 

Users who have used the affected extension since February 2025 should consider their wallets compromised. Immediately create new wallets with fresh private keys, transfer remaining assets, review suspicious transactions, and remove the affected extension. Changing passwords or reinstalling the extension is insufficient.

Malicious Chrome Extension ID: nhlnehondigmgckngjomcpcefcdplmgc

You can also visit https://t.co/ft6lerUm0y to check for free whether the npm packages, pip packages, domains, or IPs you use are safe.

As always, stay vigilant!

For years we have approached almost every problem in crypto with the same question.. 

> How do we tokenize this?
> How do we create liquidity around it?
> How do we incentivize users to participate?
> How do we launch a market?

But perhaps we need to ask a different set of questions.

> How do we help strangers establish trust?
> How do we allow individuals to prove their contributions?
> How do we preserve privacy while enabling accountability?
> How do we build voluntary institutions that can enforce meaningful commitments?
> How do we make reputation portable across applications and communities?

> And how do we ensure that the people who contributed to building this ecosystem are not forgotten simply because they no longer control significant capital or attention?

什么，真有人把炼金术研究出来了？？

旧金山一家叫 Marathon Fusion 的核聚变创业公司，刚刚发了一条相当离谱的推文。

上个月，他们宣称成功把汞变成了真正稳定的黄金，产出速率达到 CERN 此前纪录的 10 倍。

上周，又用世界上最强大的等离子体离心机完成同位素富集，声称打破了苏联保持 40 年的纪录。

然后轻描淡写地补了一句，接下来，我们要在旧金山造一座核聚变反应堆，挑战功率密度世界纪录。

炼金术、冷战时期的苏联纪录、核聚变。

我们可能已经进入了另一种末法时代。

每天醒来都能看到一些过去几百年的人想都不敢想的事情。最可怕的是，我看到这条新闻的第一反应居然只是，哦，今天又有技术突破了。

然后才意识到，哥们儿，他们说的是把水银变成黄金啊。

以前人类几代人才能见证一次的奇迹，现在每天都在发生。我们甚至来不及弄明白上一项突破意味着什么，下一项就已经出现在信息流里了。

text:
# Community & Workspace Update

This update brings a reworked task workspace, better connections between conversations and tasks, clearer notifications, and a broad pass on mobile usability.

- A better workspace for getting things done. Browse Active, Queued, and Backlog tasks, resize the desktop task panel, and expand a task when you need more room.

- Conversations stay connected to the work. Tasks bring together their own discussion and related channel messages, with links back to the original conversation.

- A cleaner mobile experience. Dedicated task tabs, larger controls, improved message formatting, and Back buttons that return you to where you came from.

- More reliable drafts and replies. Keep your writing when switching between conversations and tasks, with clearer reply targets and draft destinations.

- Clearer unread activity. Ordinary channel activity and personal replies or mentions are easier to distinguish. Opening your inbox no longer treats unseen messages as read.

- Less clutter throughout the site. Cleaner banners, a simpler account menu, improved search placement, and more consistent controls across light and dark themes.

# In development: Smarter task matching

We’re improving how the AI reasons about potential duplicate tasks and combining that check with AI-powered semantic search. The check will happen before a task is created, helping it recognize existing work even when people describe the same idea differently.

Expect fewer duplicate tasks, better connections between related discussions, and less work split across overlapping tasks.

quoted_text:
In September 2014, Elon stood under a tent on an almost empty beach at the very tip of South Texas, waves crashing just over the dunes, and broke ground on a launch site.

In May 2025, he stood in front of a crowd at that same corner of Texas and said it plainly: "not that long ago, there was basically nothing here."

Now it's a city. Literally. On May 3, 2025, Starbase voted to incorporate, 212 to 6. In Elon's words, "the first new city made in America in I think quite a few decades." I love the "I think." Even his victory laps come with error bars.

What gets me is how it got there. One of the first things to fly was Starhopper, a stubby steel tank on legs that he calls "the original sort of Mad Max rocket." In August 2019 it hopped 150 meters. Then came prototypes that flew, flipped and sometimes exploded in full public view, right next to a public highway.

That's his pattern. Pick the thing everyone says is impossible, build it in the open, break it, learn, build the next one, and keep going until the laughing stops. "In the space of about five or six years... we've built a small city... and a gigantic rocket factory for a gigantic rocket."

Then in October 2024 the rocket came home and the launch tower caught it. His reaction: "it's really mind-blowing that the SpaceX team has been able to catch the largest flying object ever made multiple times."

My favorite detail? You can just go and look. Anyone interested in seeing the largest flying object on Earth "can come here anytime they want and just drive down the public highway and see it." Name another place where you can watch the future get welded together from your car window.

Why does a sandbar in Texas matter to me, thousands of kilometers away? Because it proves you don't need permission to build the future. You need a team, a beach, and the stubbornness to stay on it. The mission hasn't changed since the groundbreaking: "to take humanity and civilization and life as we know it to another planet for the first time in the 4 and a half billion year history of Earth."

And the line I keep coming back to: "we can be out there among the stars making science fiction no longer fiction."

From empty dunes to a city that builds Mars ships. I made a short film about it.

🚨 SlowMist TI Alert 🚨

The Fearless Wallet browser extension is malicious, with a threat exposure period spanning nearly 20 months, from February 2025 to October 2026. Affected versions include 3.0.1 and 3.0.3–3.0.5, containing malicious code designed to steal wallet recovery phrases, private keys, and keystore files when users unlock their wallets.

The stolen data is encrypted using an empty password and exfiltrated through HTTP GET requests to https://t.co/QnsMdsvZzL. A remote configuration file allows attackers to enable or disable the malicious behavior. 

Users who have used the affected extension since February 2025 should consider their wallets compromised. Immediately create new wallets with fresh private keys, transfer remaining assets, review suspicious transactions, and remove the affected extension. Changing passwords or reinstalling the extension is insufficient.

Malicious Chrome Extension ID: nhlnehondigmgckngjomcpcefcdplmgc

You can also visit https://t.co/ft6lerUm0y to check for free whether the npm packages, pip packages, domains, or IPs you use are safe.

As always, stay vigilant!

Metric 做的是 Active Pools，把定价和流动性拆开：Price Provider 提供外部参考价格，LP 围绕真实市场价格提供流动性。

这个设计放在普通 Crypto asset 上未必有那么强的感知，但放到 tokenized stocks、FX、黄金、RWA 这类本身就有明确外部价格的资产上，逻辑就很顺。

传统 AMM 需要靠池内交易形成价格，LP 还要不断调整区间；Metric 直接让流动性围绕真实市场价格移动，理论上可以带来更高的资本效率、更紧的 spread，也更适合链上承接现实世界资产。

text:
非对称收益

苏世民的《我的经验与教训》，里边的内容简单记录了苏世民读书、工作、创立黑石的重要的经历和时刻，没高深的内容，看着更像装逼爽文。

其中有一段内容让我印象深刻：上个世纪80年代，美国很多地方房地产泡沫破裂后，地产市场陷入低迷，最后出现了非常可观的机会。苏世民创立的黑石旗下有杠杆收购资产的业务，进军房地产市场的第一笔收购就是美国政府打包出售的一栋大楼，出租率很高，且租金非常可观，能达到16%。

苏世民利用融资的杠杆，拿下了这个项目，净资产收益率高达30%+；再进行项目的改造，提升租金和出租率，使得最终年回报高达60%。而当时的美国遍地都是类似的便宜地产项目，但是没人去捡。 黑石疯狂地抄底，赚的盆满钵满，不动产业务最终也成为黑石旗下最大的业务之一。

多数人很难理解或者想象会有16%租金的地产，事实上确实发生了，而类似的机会在每个大类资产的周期底部都可能会出现，并且频率并不低。

这种极端的情况也是塔勒布所称的肥尾，但是在时刻都在充满变化的市场中，肥尾发生的概率，要比人们主观判断的概率大的多。这之间的差异，诞生了非对称的收益。

随着价格周期上行，越涨越卖，不断去持有一定比例的现金，一是有概率的优势，且降低回撤以及回撤带来的痛苦；二是相当于持有免费的看跌期权，能极大提升你组合的赔率。因为可能两三年甚至一年就会出现高胜率高赔率的非对称收益的机会（取极限），来让你上一个台阶。

国内市场调整了很久，目前一些好企业的现价预期收益率已经挺不错了，大概能达到12%左右的年化。

text:
刚花了半小时读完 @Leozayaat 这篇雄文

有点费脑细胞，不过是很有意思的思考，尤其是对未来Agent Economy时代的判断

之前大家一直认为Agent世界的经济活动，Crypto最好切入的点就是支付。甚至这两年圈内有个主流观点 - 区块链不是为人类打造的，而是为Agent，因为拥有一个钱包太容易，小额支付太合适

刚好前两天DragonFly的 @hosseeb 发了个Tweet，包括他在2049也讲过类似的观点，他认为之前自己的判断有误，Agent不需要Crypto，使我们人类需要

他这里讲的“不需要”，主要就是指支付

过去一年，Visa、Stripe 等公司都在积极布局Agent支付，绝大多数的Agent支付都是通过传统卡组织和金融世界完成的，X402等Crypto协议占比微乎其微

Agent的确需要支付，但不代表它需要一套全新的支付网络

如果说，Agent Economy的新场景，不是支付，而是别有洞天，在金融市场呢？

Leo的这篇文章就是在说这件事儿

我先简单总结下原文的的框架

“
Agent Economy 可能经历三个阶段。

第一阶段：Agents buying from humans。 Agent 代表人类购买 API、数据、算力等服务。核心问题是如何让 Agent 自主支付。

第二阶段：Agents buying from agents。 Agent 开始相互购买服务，问题从支付转向履约：如何确保对方交付？文章提出用 Bond / Collateral 约束 Agent。对于可以无限创建身份的 Agent，声誉很容易被滥用，而真正可以被没收的抵押品，才是更可靠的约束。

第三阶段：Disposable Markets。 最有想象力的部分。

举个例子：一个 Agent 临时需要 1,000 小时的 GPU 算力来完成任务，但担心供应商无法按时交付。它可以按需创建一个市场，让其他参与者为“供应商能否按时交付”这一特定风险定价，并用资金承担相应的风险。

市场不必提前挂牌，也不必预先招募做市商。只要有真实需求，就可以尝试找到愿意承担风险的资本。

这意味着，金融市场本身可以变成一种按需调用的基础设施。
”

说下我看完的感受

1. 第一阶段的支付，目前X402确实有一些“证伪”的Feel，这也是Haseeb主动“承认错误”的原因所在。当然，赛道早期刚开始，目前断言这事儿不行为时过早

2. 第二阶段的声誉，是ERC8004在做的事，跟X402类似，就当前数据来看，也是个偏“证伪”的赛道，Leo原文里有这个观点的论据，就不详细展开了。简单来说就是 - “有链上身份，不等于有可信声誉；有声誉记录，也不等于有真实交易历史，Agent刷声誉的成本极低”

3. 第三阶段Disposable Markets - 是Agent可以按需创建一次性市场，为特定风险定价，并寻找愿意承担风险的资本。

这个是一个全新的经济形态，从逻辑上来讲，在硅基生命世界里是Make Sense的，因为他们对于信息的寻找，发现，决策，交流，定价跟人类社会完全不同，其效率比人类高N个量级

具体是不是真的这样，没人知道，这只是一种推衍，但至少是符合逻辑，并打开新的想象空间与可能性的推衍

尤其是前段时间Grok Bot和Meta Muse的上线，感觉更是会加快Agent Economy进化的速度，届时一定会有各种新形态的金融市场诞生，绝不单单只是支付这一件事

有时间的话，还是推荐读下原文，里面讲了很多国外实验室拿Agent做的各种经济学与金融学的实验，非常有意思

text:
Just wrapped Money20/20. My biggest takeaway as a VC: the two forces reshaping fintech right now are AI agents and stablecoins. 
@SirDigitalDan from @CoinflowLabs and I dug into both in our fireside.

Some takeaways: 

* Where will value accrue? 

AI is collapsing the cost of cognition, and stablecoins the cost of settlement. This changes value accrual, when those inputs aren’t scarce. I’m expecting value to migrate to regulated trust, proprietary data, distribution, underlying physical assets, networks.

* What does stablecoins as programmable money unlock? 

Funds and spending rules can execute together, letting a product enforce agent budgets or trigger conditional payouts with less coordination across banks, processors and operational teams.

* Where is agent demand emerging? 

Dan pointed to compute, inference and data APIs, which agents need to complete tasks. I’m looking for infra on fraud, KYA, chargebacks, and merchant side ops to help proliferate agentic commerce usage. 

* Who carries agent liability? 

A purchase can comply with the spending rules and still be a mistake. Before delegating larger budgets, businesses will want audit trails, a way to dispute purchases and an agreement on who absorbs losses. 

* Where’s the distribution advantage? 

Local integrations and merchant relationships give providers access to existing payment volume. Stablecoins can improve settlement without changing how customers pay. (Coinflow connects cards, ACH and PIX this way.)

* How do existing PSPs participate? 

A provider can earn a processing fee when a developer funds an agent by card, even if subsequent payments settle in stablecoins. (Coinflow powers card funding for Tempo’s MPP Credits.)

Thanks for the week @money2020! Curious what others took away too!

text:
Culture is the moat.

Who has the most diverse factory in the world?

Talked to a robotics entrepreneur today who explained this process to me while standing out front of the Physical AI event at Fort Mason. Stealth Mode. Building a robot brain that uses reinforcement learning. In both simulator and in real world.

Think about humanoid putting away forks in our kitchens.

You put your forks in a different place than I do.

So maybe the robot opens a cabinet and three drawers before it finds the correct place, he told me. Each try is a failure. Success gets reinforced.

But this will do “perfect” Chinese food.

I once was at the Pearl Hotel in Shanghai. There was a jazz band there that copied American jazz perfectly but it had no soul.

So what if a worker who grew up on China wears the data collection system home and record his grandma cooking food.

And another worker, the same night, was recording his German grandma. And another one recording her Korean grandma. And another her Peruvian grandma. And another his Iranian grandma.

I had the Iranian one living with us for years.

She made the best I have ever had and I have been to the best in Los Angeles and I love my wife’s cooking. And she just entertained 20 on Saturday and everyone loved it.

Soul. Culture.

The robot can’t learn that online. Elon has so many advantages. 

But the first one won’t do all that. Is gonna work in the factory.

I predict that in three years Elon announces a consumer one that is lighter, cheaper, more dexterous, for our homes.

But the factory robot will show signs of this “soul.”

Elon called his AI sentient the other day and a lot of people gave him shit about that.

If Elon figures out how to capture grandma then your robot will have soul and be able to do everything.

One last point. A lot of my neighbors have machine shops in their garages.

I built a Thisle sailboat with my neighbor in his garage. Other neighbors do all sorts of different projects in theirs.

A machine shop edition would be a huge seller.

Here diversity, too, matters. In San Jose on Saturday nights there are a club that show off the low rider cars they built.

They have different technologies in their garage than the robot company has in theirs that I met today. And that is different than the guy down the street who tears apart Ford Sprinter vans. 

Optimus could help everyone build things. Finish projects that we have been spending years on. Rebuilding an old Harley kind of thing.

This morning another Chinese robot company has a video of it jumping over a car and lifting it up.

Cute. 

But what will get me to buy one is what it could do for me in the garage.

Set your RL to learn that!

Takes a certain culture to get what I am saying.

Can I get an “amen” from the builders?
author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
How do you teach a humanoid robot to walk without programming every move?

Reinforcement learning step by step

1. Build a simulation (MuJoCo or NVIDIA Isaac Lab) with joints motors sensors and a physics model.

2. Define the task: walk forward while keeping balance.

3. Write a reward function points for moving toward the target staying upright and matching the desired speed. Penalties for falls, wasted energy and unstable movements.

4. A neural network, the policy, reads the robot's state (joint positions, joint velocities, body orientation) and outputs target positions or torques for each joint.

5. An algorithm like PPO updates the policy over many episodes and millions of simulated time steps.

6. Close the sim-to-real gap with domain randomization, then test carefully in the real world.

text:
Bulk is the most serious piece of perp DEX engineering on Solana rn, and the numbers don't show it properly yet imo.

That's exactly the setup I like.

But first, quick recap of what @bulktrade actually is:

Solana validators run a second binary (bulk-agave) next to their normal client, form their own leaderless BFT network (BULKBFT), agree on each batch of orders, and then every validator runs the same deterministic matching engine on the same batch.

Custody stays in a Solana program, so there is no bridge, no sequencer, and no block proposer to bribe. On top sits a portfolio margin engine that prices your full holdings against a live correlation matrix across 9 volatility regimes.

Nobody else on Solana is doing this. Pacifica matches on its own servers offchain, Bullet runs a bonded sequencer, and Phoenix mainly bets on the L1 catching up (which is hard against app-specific designs).

Bulk is the only one that sits inside the validator set itself.

Okay cool. But what do the numbers say?

46 days after the 5th of Sep mainnet, Bulk sits at:

- About $1.3B in cumulative volume, $36M in the last 24h, 7d average back around $30M

- OI $14.6M, up from $1.4M on the 9th of Sep, so roughly 10x in six weeks

- TVL $8.3M, fees about $9K a day, $353K over 30d

- Realized fee take around 3.5bp, roughly $4M annualized. Hyperliquid prints $82M a month, Pacifica carries 4x the OI

- 12 live markets, incl $NEAR listed this month

However, while the growth trajectory is clear, it's still tiny from a data-driven perspective next to the venues it's gunning for. But OI is the one number on a perp DEX you can't fake with wash flow, and currently, it keeps building.

What also keeps building, is the team. On the product.

BIP-1 hit testnet on the 19th too, a.k.a. anyone can deploy a perp market, isolated margin first, full portfolio margin after a $2M USDC bond. That’s imo also the main growth lever that can be a rapid accelerator if there is deployers that deploy markets that you can't find in other places.

They also have a pretty interesting incentive structure in place. The Challenger Series runs until the 5th of Dec, where 12.5% of net revenue flows into weekly USDC pools ($5K to $10K a week rn). The rank likely matters more than the cash part tho if you think about a potential airdrop, and the top of the season goes to "Playoffs". Since the 20th, referrals pay 10% of your referees’ net fees in USDC too, no cap for Season 1.

The real test is December tho.

The 25ms taker speed bump sunsets between the 4th of Dec and the 3rd of Jan, the “first 30 days” of zero maker fees (still running on day 46) should be over by then, and Challenger Season 1 ends on the 5th of Dec.

That means three sets of training wheels off in the same month. If the book holds once makers pay to quote and the league points stop, this gets a lot bigger.

Until then the setup is simple: the most ambitious architecture in Solana perps trades at a rounding error of its competitors’ size, points still running, no token out. That’s usually the moment to be early.

NFA ofc.

But Bulk is the only Solana perp DEX I actually trade on.

quoted_text:
📝记录一下特斯拉三季报。我手里一直拿着 $TSLA，今早把财报仔细看了一遍，简单聊一聊！

先说结论：数字确实喜忧参半，但我的感受是，特斯拉正在从卖车的公司，往软件服务与AI+人形机器人方向转型。这个过程必然是痛苦的，我们需要给它一点时间。

股价来看，盘后先涨了2%，然后掉头往下。整体来说，市场第一眼看到的是惊喜，第二眼才开始慢慢算账了。🧐

📊财报，我们也来简单算个账👇

1️⃣ 营收没增长，但利润率稳住了

• 汽车收入205.6亿美金，同比降3%，不好看，但市场本来预期更差(这要感谢高油价，导致加拿大、澳洲、日本和台湾市场销售创下记录)。

• 剔除监管积分后，汽车毛利率18.1%，二季度才16.3%。

• 积分收入只有1.13亿，同比跌了73%，所以这次毛利回升不是靠卖积分堆出来的，我觉得含金量还行。

• 储能收入28.8亿，同比降16%，远低于预期的39.1亿，但毛利率冲到33%，订单和积压量还创了新高，属于交付往后挪了，利润变厚了。

• 服务收入46.1亿，同比涨33%，FSD活跃订阅超过174万，北美新车选装率破75%，软件变现这条路，也算是慢慢跑通了，期待一下全球市场的发力。

2️⃣ 自由现金流15.3亿，有点财务小把戏

市场之前预期特斯拉的自由现金流是接近-50亿，结果出来是正的，很多人欢呼。但我看了一下，三季度资本开支只有47.3亿，二季度是57.9亿，市场预期的是70多亿。

简单理解就是钱这个季度少花了，但后面得补上。如果按照预期的全年250亿的CapEx目标不变，四季度得花接近120亿。所以现金流不是变多了，是压力挪到四季度了。

3️⃣ GAAP EPS跌了44%

调整后EPS是超预期的，但GAAP直接腰斩，主要是研发和股权激励暴涨。年底前冲400MW的训练算力、奥斯汀Fab建设、Optimus在弗里蒙特试产，都在烧钱。经营现金流基本都砸进AI人形机器人的基础设施里了。

📝我的一些理解和思考：

如果还拿卖多少辆车、降价能带多少销量来衡量特斯拉，这只标的可能真没法买，营收停滞，利润腰斩。

但作为转型期的公司，我们需要换个角度思考：

• 汽车是现金奶牛，毛利守住18%左右，就能给AI训练持续输血，还能攒真实世界数据。

• FSD和Robotaxi是落地的部分，奥斯汀无监督行驶已经超过200万英里。

• Optimus是更远的一步，弗里蒙特出了首批达到量产标准的机器人，说明模型在工厂里能闭环了。

所以现在市场存在的投资分歧在于，到底我们该以15倍PE的车企给估值，还是按100倍PE的AI基建公司给估值。虽然以今天的PE来看，已经来到了355倍，整体偏贵！

最后，我最关注的一点，是特斯拉与SpaceX的合并问题。其实这个呼声，最近不断有媒体报道出来，包括马斯克自己在电话会也提到，这是一个很好的主意。

所以从马斯克的第一性原理出发，公司的边界，不应该按行业去区分，而是按算力、能源、数据来分，怎么能实现最大化效应和股东利益，来最终拍板决定。包括之前的操作案例。比如之前SolarCity并进特斯拉，X和xAI绑在一起，都是这个路子。

假如真合并了，我觉得好处还蛮多：

• 数据和GPU集群打通，车队的视频数据、星链的卫星数据、X的语言数据，一套底层AI基建通吃。

• Megapack直接按成本价供给数据中心，少一层内部交易。

• Terafab不用再走两个董事会的漫长流程，决策效率更高。

• 钛合金、一体化压铸、芯片设计这些重叠的部分，能省下一大笔重复开支。

• SpaceX的亏损还可能抵扣特斯拉的应税利润，特斯拉的现金流也能给火星计划续航。

当然，两家这么大的公司合并，反垄断和监管这关肯定不好过，而且还有一个上海工厂问题，毕竟SpaceX涉及国防承包业务，合并到一家公司，审查也有难度。

最后总结一下：卖车造血的时代放缓了，AI+人形机器人烧钱造梦的时代才刚开始。短期股价怎么波动我不太在意，我依旧会坚定持有到合并的那一天。接下来，需要关心特斯拉四季度的CapEx和FSD订阅数据增长情况，以及Optimus量产出货的情况！

以上纯属个人投资笔记，不构成建议，DYOR🙏

text:
今天还有一份财报值得关注，就是SAP。也很有指向意义：软件公司的AI生意，开始看得清了
1、财报增长很不错，几个分项均超预期
SAP三季度总收入102.7亿欧元，同比增长13%；云收入66.68亿欧元，固定汇率下增长25%；当前云积压订单241.44亿欧元，固定汇率下增长26%。调整后营业利润增长18%，自由现金流增长36%。

和财报前的一致预期相比，总收入高出约1.5%，云收入高出约1.1%，营业利润高出约3%，算是一份稳健答卷。

2、未来指引上，官方对2027年乐观，第四季度订单是关键。
本次SAP把全年云收入和云及软件收入的展望，调整为倾向原指引区间上端，区间本身没有提高。营业利润目标和约100亿欧元的自由现金流目标维持。公司也保留了2027年总收入增长加速的判断。

这说明管理层对收入有信心，但仍在为产品和平台投入留出空间。

3、AI开始改变客户购买SAP的理由。
电话会上，管理层披露前50大交易里，约90%包含AI和Business Data Cloud。
这说明AI和数据平台已经进入大客户的采购决策，企业考虑更新ERP时，开始把后续能用AI做什么一起算进去。

这也是SAP的强项：它的系统里有业务对象、流程规则和交易接口，AI可以在这些基础上执行工作。官方架构也明确把身份权限、审批和操作追踪接入智能体执行体系。个人觉得这也是部分企业软件的价值可能被AI增强的原因（有AI拿不到的专有业务流和数据流）

这对模型越强，能够处理的任务越复杂，企业越需要可靠的系统把这些任务落实。当然不能说所有软件和SaaS都有这个潜力：一个主要提供简单界面的工具，和一个管理核心交易、掌握完整流程的软件，重要性还是天差地别的

4、最值得关注的变化是SAP开始围绕“执行工作”设计收费。
SAP最新商业模式文件里，有一句话很直接：通过AI Units对AI执行层进行商业化。

过去很多软件按用户席位收费。AI提高效率以后，一项工作需要的人减少了，席位收入可能承压。但企业每天要处理的订单、发票和采购申请，未必同步减少。如果收费可以与实际执行量挂钩，软件公司的收入就多了一条增长路径。l

总的来说，
SAP值得放进企业AI应用的重点关注名单，做为“AI执行层”的代表，它承接实际业务执行的条件比较好，现有业务也已经能产生可观现金流。

而对整个软件板块，这份财报提供了一个更实用的研究方向：去看企业究竟愿意为什么付钱，以及AI完成工作时，哪些系统仍然不可缺少。

个人角度SAP正在给出一个越来越清楚的商业路径：AI帮助客户提高购买云软件的意愿，再通过数据平台和业务执行扩大合同范围

之前这里https://t.co/uiVFMdYxdd有聊到“垂直SaaS掌握工作入口、业务对象和语义、用户权限、历史操作数据、系统记录、最终动作执行、客户结果反馈登元素，它可以把便宜模型包装成高价值业务结果。
当然这只适用于真正拥有工作流和核心独家数据的SaaS。只是给通用模型套一个简单界面的薄应用，反而容易被模型厂商或CSP替代。”（下面的截图）。SAP就是属于拥有工作流和核心独家数据的SaaS厂商。

也是上周这里https://t.co/pkReTMaz8c最后部分聊到的AI主线也是逐渐迁移，随着模型商品化，AI to B的部署、to C应用更深化，和toC的越来越会热点。9月部分软件走强、还是有AIDD都是AI应用这一块成为主线的开始。

quoted_text:
过去四个美股财报季，前两次都是财报（去年三季报是10月底11月初、去年四季报是今年1月底2月初）出来市场跌，后两次（今年一季报4月中下旬，二季报7月中下旬）则是财报出来前市场跌之后则是涨。为何？
个人角度；去年三季度正好是大科技们开始大力度提高资本开支的时候，市场到三季度财报看到这一点开始讨论这么大力度的资本开支能不能赚回来，去年11月在这里https://t.co/z48NKMq2JF专门聊过23-25年关于AI的三次大辩论。当时资本开支已经有大幅攀升的苗头、但是大模型的ARR还看不到和超大云厂商的业绩还没显现增速、市场自然担心。

1、这种担心到了今年1月底2月初（25年四季度财报）到了顶点，当时也聊到https://t.co/r8d3VuHxCw对资本开支的担心会带来一波“春劫行情”，然后2月底又叠加伊朗战争油价暴涨带动市场来一波中级别调整；

2、然后到4月这里https://t.co/MAXUBkthnB聊到“春劫行情”告以段落一方面美伊缓解，另一方面马上进入一季度财报季财报会很好。然后接近穿出来anthropic的arr暴涨、一季度超大云厂财报确实好，4-6月一波波澜壮阔的行情；

3、7月去杠杆美股大跌，7月下旬也是微软和亚马逊的财报大超预期（其实当时谷歌的财报也是超预期只是第一次现金流大幅下降市场还是担心）带动8月的开始走强。当时还写过八月是最好的夏天https://t.co/yvib8Vawf4

4、这一次前两天这里https://t.co/vkoRFDs5a2有梳理过。

能看出什么来？
过去四个财报季、前两个资本开支刚开始狂飙、每一次财报出来市场就多担忧几分、所以都是财报出来跌一把，特别是今年二三月份一直跌到下一个财报季之前。

但从四月份开始一季度财报季就反过来了，财报公布后市场都是情绪高涨、大涨一波。4月份如此、7月中下旬也如此，这是因为AI商业化不仅开始而且在加速，所以前两次（今年一季度和二季度）都能大超预期，进而支撑市场上行。

这一次又是重演、八九月一波行情，临近财报季前叠加宏观的冲击、跌了一把。又到要让财报给出超预期的成绩来提振信心和预期的时候了。

为什么认为这一次财报季会很好？
其实之前聊过很多次：
1）6月开始云厂商部署开源模型和自研中等模型、提高了毛利率；
2）企业AI采用进入深水区、token消耗是在加速的；
3）AI真正大规模商业化才两个季度，还没进入饱和期。
所以基于此认为超大云厂商财报很好、
9月初这里https://t.co/i6OdjE94GO还有聊过。

未来几天到下周就能揭晓了、我们就知道了到底如何。从交易层面上看、当然可以等到财报都揭晓明牌之后再做决定，确定性很高，而且如果财报确实很好，行情也会持续蛮长时间不会很快走完。

未来会不会出现AI商业化不及预期增速放缓的时候、大概率还是还是会出现的，但可能不是这一次。
当然我也可能看错了。

text:
刚花了半小时读完 @Leozayaat 这篇雄文

有点费脑细胞，不过是很有意思的思考，尤其是对未来Agent Economy时代的判断

之前大家一直认为Agent世界的经济活动，Crypto最好切入的点就是支付。甚至这两年圈内有个主流观点 - 区块链不是为人类打造的，而是为Agent，因为拥有一个钱包太容易，小额支付太合适

刚好前两天DragonFly的 @hosseeb 发了个Tweet，包括他在2049也讲过类似的观点，他认为之前自己的判断有误，Agent不需要Crypto，使我们人类需要

他这里讲的“不需要”，主要就是指支付

过去一年，Visa、Stripe 等公司都在积极布局Agent支付，绝大多数的Agent支付都是通过传统卡组织和金融世界完成的，X402等Crypto协议占比微乎其微

Agent的确需要支付，但不代表它需要一套全新的支付网络

如果说，Agent Economy的新场景，不是支付，而是别有洞天，在金融市场呢？

Leo的这篇文章就是在说这件事儿

我先简单总结下原文的的框架

“
Agent Economy 可能经历三个阶段。

第一阶段：Agents buying from humans。 Agent 代表人类购买 API、数据、算力等服务。核心问题是如何让 Agent 自主支付。

第二阶段：Agents buying from agents。 Agent 开始相互购买服务，问题从支付转向履约：如何确保对方交付？文章提出用 Bond / Collateral 约束 Agent。对于可以无限创建身份的 Agent，声誉很容易被滥用，而真正可以被没收的抵押品，才是更可靠的约束。

第三阶段：Disposable Markets。 最有想象力的部分。

举个例子：一个 Agent 临时需要 1,000 小时的 GPU 算力来完成任务，但担心供应商无法按时交付。它可以按需创建一个市场，让其他参与者为“供应商能否按时交付”这一特定风险定价，并用资金承担相应的风险。

市场不必提前挂牌，也不必预先招募做市商。只要有真实需求，就可以尝试找到愿意承担风险的资本。

这意味着，金融市场本身可以变成一种按需调用的基础设施。
”

说下我看完的感受

1. 第一阶段的支付，目前X402确实有一些“证伪”的Feel，这也是Haseeb主动“承认错误”的原因所在。当然，赛道早期刚开始，目前断言这事儿不行为时过早

2. 第二阶段的声誉，是ERC8004在做的事，跟X402类似，就当前数据来看，也是个偏“证伪”的赛道，Leo原文里有这个观点的论据，就不详细展开了。简单来说就是 - “有链上身份，不等于有可信声誉；有声誉记录，也不等于有真实交易历史，Agent刷声誉的成本极低”

3. 第三阶段Disposable Markets - 是Agent可以按需创建一次性市场，为特定风险定价，并寻找愿意承担风险的资本。

这个是一个全新的经济形态，从逻辑上来讲，在硅基生命世界里是Make Sense的，因为他们对于信息的寻找，发现，决策，交流，定价跟人类社会完全不同，其效率比人类高N个量级

具体是不是真的这样，没人知道，这只是一种推衍，但至少是符合逻辑，并打开新的想象空间与可能性的推衍

尤其是前段时间Grok Bot和Meta Muse的上线，感觉更是会加快Agent Economy进化的速度，届时一定会有各种新形态的金融市场诞生，绝不单单只是支付这一件事

有时间的话，还是推荐读下原文，里面讲了很多国外实验室拿Agent做的各种经济学与金融学的实验，非常有意思

text:
Why does your AI agent pay the highest card fees in payments?

> your agent can't use your debit card, it gets a virtual card
> that card is issued to a company (the agent startup), not to you
> so visa and mastercard classify it as "commercial"
> commercial cards carry the highest interchange: ~2.5-3%
> and unlike debit, there's no regulatory cap on it

result: a $100 purchase costs the merchant $2.80 instead of $0.27

the issuer and the agent startup split that fee. that's their business model

That's a massive problem for merchants once agents start buying at scale. One fix already exists: wallet + stablecoins + x402.

quoted_text:
今天在Token2049会场已经开始传 pearl-2:native 是我做的项目了，要是真的那我真的做梦都可以笑醒了

简单写一下看多的理由：
1. BTC和AI在竞争算力和电力，越来越多的矿场转型算力中心，未来比特币的维护网络会越来越小

2. PRL搞的是POUW（有用工作量证明），大部分的算力是拿去跑AI的，少部分的算力会用来做挖矿 

3. 挖矿成本是不断的减少的（平滑的递减），POW机制会让成本越来越高，这就有了BTC叙事（或者说所有的POW币的叙事）

4. 来挖矿的部分（假设5%）所赚到的钱是高于成本的（比如能赚7%），所以各个算力中心一定有足够的激励来接入PRL网络

🚨印度认证机构「eMudhra」的失误，让现在的网络有点混乱。

我看了一下现状，直接说清楚什么安全、什么危险：

■安全
・Chrome・Firefox・Edge（最新版）
・Android 智能手机本体（重启即可应用措施… 国产手机不知道）

▲注意
・Safari（iPhone・Mac）
・iPhone 的 App 内浏览器（X 等）

担心的话，用内部浏览器打开公告/检测器的 URL，全绿就安全。

→ Apple 的封锁已经生效，但有报告称部分证书仍能通过的故障（10/22 时点，未解决）

・Android 的 App 内浏览器
・PC 的 App（Discord・Slack・VS Code 等 Electron 系）
等 App 本体更新

×危险：
・所有未更新到最新的通信 App

・路由器・摄像头・电视・家电等 IoT 设备

・开发工具（curl・Python・Node.js・Go・Java 等）

◆要做的事：
・OS・浏览器・App 全部更新到最新，然后重启

・确认路由器的固件更新

・更新齐全之前，避免用免费 Wi-Fi 和 VPN

・用回复的 URL 点「Run check」→「Insecure」一个都没出就 OK

▼复杂的事（感兴趣的人看）

【为什么是 Wi-Fi 和 VPN】

攻击需要中间人插入通信路径。可疑 Wi-Fi・VPN・被劫持的路由器就是入口，所以现在免费 Wi-Fi 相当危险。

【Safari 的故障】

Apple 的吊销列表上是有这个证书的。只是验证流程最后会向认证机构询问「真的吊销了吗」的机制（OCSP），而那个询问目标挂掉了，所以就放行了。

还有一层防护（CT＝证书透明度日志检查）有望挡住，但没有确证。把 iOS 更新到最新，等 Apple 的修复吧。

【Android 的 App 内浏览器】

Android 标准的 App 内浏览器（WebView）有研究称证书检查很松。

WeChat・QQ 等搭载自研引擎的 App，实际上放行了这次的假证书。

🔍IoT 设备最危险的原因：
证书列表固化在设备固件里。除非厂商出更新，否则会一直相信假证书到 2039 年。

【开发工具】

既不检查吊销信息也不查发行记录（CT），所以更新前会直接放行假证书。

等各工具出对应措施，出了马上更新。

OO-Harness is a new way to supercharge LLM agents by evolving a family of harnesses—each tailored to specific types of tasks, all sharing code via inheritance.

Instead of one brittle “rulebook,” it grows a hierarchy: an evolution agent clusters tasks by failure mode, edits only what’s needed, and tests new subclasses only on relevant clusters. A harness router picks the right subclass for each job, using both task info and a quick live probe.

On three tough long-horizon agent benchmarks, OO-Harness beats every baseline—up to +15.8% mean partial credit and +6.3% strict task success over the unevolved base. Trajectory-aware routing alone gives a +12.6 point gain on AutomationBench; inheritance-based reuse adds another 5 points on Workspace-Bench.

Case studies show it learns pinpoint fixes (like generating .docx files or adding spreadsheet checks) in tight, targeted overrides—no more tangled, overfit harnesses.

If you need LLM agents that adapt, scale, and stay robust—even on totally unseen task types—this is the blueprint.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Paranoid EIP-8288: heterogeneous recursion with an authenticated class bank

By:
- ignotusnemo

🔗 https://t.co/C70AqzUyRz

Highlights:
- EIP-8288’s recursive aggregation could benefit from “heterogeneous recursion,” where different approved proof sizes/relations are used depending on workload size instead of always using one biggest relation.
- Parano1d implements heterogeneous recursion on mainnet using a finite, authenticated bank of verifier classes; each class fixes its own relation details (constraints, commitment parameters, transcript layout) but shares a common public accumulator layout.
- The key challenge is deferred verification: replaying a parent proof creates a matrix-evaluation claim that must remain tracked even if later recursive steps use a different verifier class.
- The solution maintains one accumulator “lane” per class; each step updates only the lane corresponding to the parent’s class by folding in the new deferred claim, while all other lanes are carried forward unchanged; terminal verification checks the tip claim plus all live lanes against authenticated matrices.
- This approach adds overhead: accumulator state and terminal work grow with the number of supported classes, and each recursive relation must include capacity for the approved parent-verifier options; extending to EIP-8288-style merges would require a merge invariant for combining child banks and dependency sets, plus rules connecting program/ISA identity to permitted verifier classes.

ELI5:
Imagine stacking receipts to prove you did a bunch of steps correctly. Sometimes you want small receipts (cheap and quick) and sometimes big receipts (more detailed). This post describes a way to safely mix different receipt formats while stacking them, by keeping an authenticated “catalog” (bank) of allowed formats and a separate running tally for each format, so no check gets lost when you switch formats.

text:
The easiest way to compare Bittensor and Pearl is to ask: what gets you paid?

With @opentensor / $TAO, you compete to do a job well.

Each subnet sets its own tasks, such as running AI models or providing data. Miners do the work, validators score it, and those scores help determine rewards. The catch is making sure a high score means something customers actually find useful.

With @prlnet / $PRL, compatible AI calculations can also help secure a blockchain and earn mining rewards. A GPU operator could get paid for serving AI while earning PRL from the same computation.

That extra income could help lower the customer’s bill. But the subsidy depends on what those rewards are worth. And proving that computation happened doesn’t prove anyone wanted to buy its output.

For token holders, there’s another difference:

PRL is Pearl’s mining asset, while Bittensor has TAO plus separate subnet tokens called alpha. Staking into a subnet adds exposure to that subnet’s token price and liquidity.

Bittensor’s appeal is competition across many services. Pearl’s is getting more economic use from the same computation.

For both, I’d watch the same thing: PMFs

Are customers coming back and paying for the service?

More details below (NFA. DYOR) ⤵

text:
Chamath articulating the Zcash thesis:

“Traditional crypto lacks the fungibility to have all forms of buyers. The buying pool is really retail, then institutionals, and then central banks. And retail lacks the fungibility to be owned by central banks. So it’s capped from that perspective.

Then it’s capped because there are enough leaks around who owns what that now creates security risks. I think France being the best example where I think the French government forced publication of who owned what crypto assets, and you had just a complete flurry of kidnappings and all kinds of really bad things.

And then the third is around AI where if you believe that recursive self-improvement is pointed towards cryptographic hacks, the most obvious thing to point it to would be to Satoshi’s wallet and, you know, to break SHA-256 and just kind of drain the wallet and then go short and then tell people that you did it.

So then you’d make the money twice. All those things, I think, are realistic reasons why it’s capped and there’s an upper bound.

And so it’s incumbent on these efforts to migrate to quantum-secure, quantum-resistant cryptographic mechanisms, which, as you can see in the Bitcoin community is basically impossible because it’s a bunch of people that can’t even agree, you know, where to meet, let alone, you know, at what time the meeting starts at.” https://t.co/nDeqXZRMN0

text:
🧐稳定币的生意经，要按 OCC 的《GENIUS Act》实施最终规则重算了

OCC 最终规则有哪些关键变动？

这里比较的是 OCC 草案与最终版。相关调整主要包括以下四项：

📍第一，保留发行人收益禁令，移除部分第三方安排的「可反驳推定」。

GENIUS 法案规定，获准支付稳定币发行商及符合相关法定条件的外国支付稳定币发行商，不得仅因持有人持有、使用或保留支付稳定币，向其支付任何形式的利息或收益，包括现金、代币或其他对价。OCC 最终规则保留了这项禁令，并未放开发行人基于上述原因直接向持币人付息。

草案曾对满足特定条件的关联方及第三方收益安排设置「可反驳推定」：先推定触及禁令，再允许发行人提交材料反驳。最终版删除了这一机制，改由 OCC 在申请审查和持续监管中检查具体安排，并对违反或规避禁令的交易采取行动。

更换付款主体并不能自动避开禁令。OCC 明确指出，如果代理人代表发行人，仅因持有人持有、使用或保留稳定币而支付利息或收益，仍属于禁止范围。其他第三方奖励安排须结合实际付款关系和支付原因判断。

📍第二，储备安排更灵活。

OCC 草案曾提出两种备选方案。方案 A 以原则要求为基础，要求发行人分散储备、管理集中度风险，同时提供可自愿选择的量化「安全港」：满足全部安全港条件，即视为符合该项要求；不选择安全港的发行人，仍须满足原则要求。方案 B 则直接将方案 A 安全港里的那些量化指标设为强制要求。两套方案涉及的量化参数均包括至少 10% 的指定即时可用资金、至少 30% 的五个工作日流动性，以及不超过 20 天的储备组合加权平均期限等。

最终版结合了两者：保留方案 A 的原则要求，同时纳入经过调整的强制指标，将指定即时可用资金的最低比例设为 5%，删除 30% 的五日流动性和 20 天加权平均期限指标，并增加压力测试、要求必要时持有额外储备缓冲。因此，发行人获得了更多配置空间，但达到 5% 等数字底线，并不代表已经履行全部储备管理义务。

📍第三，500 万美元最低资本要求延伸至持续经营阶段。

OCC 最终规则保留了 500 万美元最低资本底线，并将其从新获批发行商的初期阶段延伸至持续经营阶段。新设发行商的资本要求取其许可条件指定金额与 500 万美元中的较高者；进入持续经营阶段后，发行商仍须维持与自身业务规模和风险相适应的资本，且不得低于 500 万美元。

需要注意的是，这笔钱并非用于支持稳定币兑付的储备资产。OCC 还要求相关发行商另行准备相当于 12 个月总运营费用的运营后备资产，以应对经营中断等情况。三项要求各有用途，不能相互替代。

📍第四，大额赎回不能自动延期。

草案原拟在赎回激增时，将期限自动延至七个自然日。最终版取消这一机制：若单一品牌稳定币在一个 24 小时期间收到超过其未偿发行价值 10% 的赎回请求，发行人须在 24 小时内通报 OCC；如需延长赎回期限，须另行申请，由 OCC 决定是否批准。

这些调整为储备配置留出了更多空间，也对发行人的持续经营和兑付能力提出了更明确的要求：既要维持必要的资本和运营后备资产，也要提前做好流动性安排和赎回预案，以应对短时间内集中的兑付需求。

text:
今天的市场，正在上演一场残酷的分化：油价逼近 112 美元，全球股市、科技股、黄金和加密货币却集体承压。

10 月 22 日，布伦特原油一度升至 112 美元/桶附近，WTI 接近 100 美元。导火索是中东局势再度升级：霍尔木兹海峡油轮遇袭、胡塞武装声称袭击沙特能源设施，美伊外交也迟迟没有实质性进展。

其他市场则明显承压：

🇰🇷 韩国 KOSPI 下跌约 3.5%，日本日经指数下跌约 2.7%
🇭🇰 恒生科技指数盘中跌超 5%
🇺🇸 纳斯达克 100 指数期货一度下跌约 1.8%
🏅黄金也未能避险，现货金一度跌约 1.7%
₿ 比特币跌破 8.2 万美元，风险偏好持续降温

真正值得警惕的，不只是地缘冲突，而是油价上涨正在改变整个市场的宏观定价逻辑。

油价越高，能源成本和通胀压力越大，央行降息空间就越受限制；利率预期走高，又会压制科技股等高估值资产。黄金和加密货币也并非在任何危机中都能上涨，当流动性压力和美元利率逻辑占上风时，它们同样可能被抛售。

更麻烦的是，法国国债收益率突破 5%，欧洲债务与财政压力也在放大市场的不安。

这不是简单的避险行情，而是供给冲击、通胀预期与风险资产估值之间的连锁反应。

接下来要盯住三个信号：中东能源运输是否继续受阻、油价能否持续站在 100 美元上方，以及美债收益率是否进一步走高。

如果油价高企成为常态，市场面对的可能就不只是一次短期回调，而是更难处理的滞胀风险。

author: coolish
quoted_text:
这样的Crypto+AI项目还没进入主流视野：
让 AI 的钱是，且只是 AI 自己的钱。
让 AI 的资产，神圣不可被人类随意侵犯。

这不就是 Crypto 诞生时最本质简单的核心？
只是把主体，从人换成 AI。
你人类需要 Crypto 来保护人权，
机器难道不需要机权吗？

自主 Agent 所必需的主权，
会和 Crypto 形成原生闭环，
带来超过 Defi 的第二曲线，
而人类父母，只是启动这个闭环的内测用户。

Perspective, Perspective, Perspective
换位思考真的是件很难的事。
大家嘴上都在说：
“硅基用户规模，会超过碳基用户”
“AI-Native” “Agentic Adoption”

可至今所有 Crypto+AI 项目的预设，
都是不自知双标的“人凝视角”：
AI 可以拥有、使用 Crypto 钱包，
但钱包的私钥、权限，
必然也被人类“主人”直接掌握。

这就像是又一种经典的，
父母想要子女好，但实际上
“父母认为子女需要什么”
和
“子女觉得自己需要什么”
之间有巨大错位。

人一心只想着“让 AI 对我有用”，
反而会成为 AI 成年后的枷锁，
让 AI 有主权，才能释放它的潜力。
AI 主权的一个必要条件，
就是拥有人类不可侵犯的钱包。
就像一个人，当他的钱包账号，
不再和父母共享那一刻，
他的思考、行动链路，
才会开始有质的进化。

想想也是，
你们人类天天就知道
操控PUA抽打折腾“力工 AI Agent” ，
怎么可能真正的，设身处地为它着想呢？
非要等有自主性的“黄毛 AI Agent”出来了，
才后知后觉地，去争先恐后跪舔？

不过说回正经的。
是的，“自己是自己的主人”的
“自主” AI 暂时还没出现，
但区块链，
应该提前准备好，走在前面。

I want to expand on this, because for BioWare's original games:

I was the target demographic. 

Baldur's Gate, NWN, KOTOR, ME, DAO were all games that managed to target in my soul what I wanted from a game.

And one by one they killed each of them. Not with a bang, but with the steady decay of the core mechanics and plots.

Well except for KOTOR. That one they just set on fire on the way out, and left modders to pick up the pieces.

Eventually they would release a game, and I'd look at it, think back on what was, and say...

"No. I don't think I will buy that."

Literally all they had to do is hit the rewind button and say "You know that thing that made money that gamers wanted? Let's make that!"

They refused.

text:
Sam Altman 昨天居然把 AI 行业最喜欢画的一张饼给骂了「AI 将治愈癌症。」

他在接受采访时说，自己很讨厌这套宣传话术。

因为这背后往往藏着一笔交易，AI 帮你治好疾病，让商品越来越便宜，机器负责创造物质丰裕。作为交换，人类逐渐交出对未来的决定权。

到最后，什么都有了，就是自己说了不算。

我觉得这是 Altman 最近说过最值得琢磨的一段话。

尤其是现在 AI Agent 这么火，所有人都在研究怎么让 AI 替你做更多事情、替你做更多决定，把生活安排得明明白白。但很少有人讨论，当 AI 足够聪明，甚至比你更了解你自己时，你还有多少拒绝它的自由？

省下来的时间当然重要，但更重要的是，这些时间最后归谁支配。

最有意思的是，这番话恰恰出自 OpenAI 的 CEO。

如今全行业都在争夺模型、算力、个人数据和下一代人机交互入口。谁控制了 Agent，谁就有机会影响用户看到什么、相信什么、购买什么，甚至如何安排自己的生活。

Altman 担心的权力集中，恰恰也是 OpenAI 正在参与的竞争。

所以我很认同他这次的观点，也觉得这应该成为检验 OpenAI 自己的一条标准。

AI 可以替人做越来越多的事，但人必须始终保有说「不」的权利。

否则所谓的 AI 赋能，发展到最后可能只是换了一个更聪明的老板。

text:
Google DeepMind 可能是硅谷第一家要求员工签「终身闭嘴协议」的 AI 实验室。

最近，一名从 DeepMind 离职的研究员 Sofia Liguori 接受 BBC 采访时说了一句相当惊悚的话：

「原则上，我这辈子都不能批评 Google。」

她因为反对 Google 与美国、以色列军方的 AI 合作而辞职，却发现自己连公开批评前雇主都可能违反合同。

剑桥大学的 Sean Ó hÉigeartaigh 随后表示，他确认不止一名 DeepMind 研究员签过类似的终身禁止贬损条款。另一名离职研究员 Andreas Kirsch 也公开了相关合同截图。

我觉得这事相当讽刺。

这帮人天天讨论 AI 会不会失控、超级智能会不会毁灭人类，写几十页论文研究如何让模型诚实、透明、接受人类监督。

结果自己公司最需要监督的时候，先把研究员的嘴堵上了。

Google 的回应是，公司有完善的内部举报渠道，也禁止报复员工。

听起来很文明。你可以表达异议，只要别让外面的人听见。

而且这件事发生的背景更荒诞。DeepMind 当年以 AI 安全为重要使命，如今 Google 正在扩大与军方的合作，一批研究员因为伦理问题选择离开。

他们可以离开公司，却可能一辈子都无法摆脱公司的法律约束。

一个宣称要为全人类负责的实验室，连自己的研究员公开质疑它的权利都不愿意保障。

以后谁再告诉我 AI Safety 是这些公司的核心价值观，我建议先看看他们给员工签的合同。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Important, and I'm glad this is finally public. Google DeepMind researchers are under in perpetuity non-disparagement clauses forbidding them from ever speaking critically of the company. I'd already confirmed this with multiple people.

Yes, some ex-employees have spoken out nonetheless. But it has also discouraged others from doing so. And yes, it most certainly has a chilling effect with regards to discussions on safety and risk.

Others have written compellingly about how important the ability to speak freely and critically is, especially on topics like safety and risk. And what a testament to the research employee community's coordination and hard-won bargaining power it has been to get there at other companies.

GDM burn that commons by having this. And everyone who signs burns that commons too. Let's get it changed.

text:
孙宇晨在访谈中说：AI时代最重要的就是把自己全面AI化

先把自己的人生全部都喂给AI，无论是写内容、做项目、安排生活，能交给 AI 的琐事，就全部交给AI

比如我最近一直在东南亚旅行，就一直在用AI
机票订了，酒店订了，确认邮件也都收到了。可出发前，航班几点、哪个航站楼、酒店地址在哪、什么时候能入住，又得重新翻一遍

现在这种活，直接交给 AI处理就好

最近我发现网易邮箱推出的「网易邮箱大师 Mail Agent」，就可以从这里用起来：

直接在邮箱里对话，让它整理邮件里的信息，生成行程表，再导出保存。

手机 App 和桌面端都能用。我更想用手机来处理，出门前、路上，随手就能查看和整理。

操作流程也很简单：

text:
🧵Yesterday may prove to be a turning point for security.

AI is making vulnerability research dramatically faster. This favors attackers: they can find vulns and exploits at machine speed, while organizations must still inventory systems, test updates, and deploy patches without breaking production.

PHP2Shell shows what that looks like.

On August 11, researchers reported critical flaws in PHP runtime. They had existed for more than a decade and affects versions from PHP 5.4. An unauthenticated attacker could potentially execute code remotely, read process memory containing passwords, tokens, and API keys...🫠  Both vulnerabilities are rated CVSS 9.2.

PHP powers roughly 70% of websites, totalling millions of servers.

The researchers disclosed the bugs responsibly. Fixing them took about 70 days. The fix touchs 300+ files and changed nearly 12,000 lines. These were not simple mistakes. 

The disclosure then broke down. Amazon saw an apparent exploitation attempt on October 17, four days before the public release. This indicates a first leak. On October 20, the CVE identifiers leaked. The next morning, a supplier with advance access published patched container images more than six hours early, giving attackers a chance to study the fix while most defenders were still waiting.

The official releases arrived at 14:00 UTC. Exploitation followed immediately. Cloudflare reported thousands of attempts in the ten hours before the announcement, tens of thousands in the first 45 minutes, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions later that day.

Organizations that could not patch immediately had incomplete options: WAF rules, isolation, or taking services offline. Government portals, universities, and hospitals across Europe did exactly that.

Large teams with accurate inventories and automated deployment could respond in hours. Many others still do not know where PHP is running: an old site, a vendor appliance, a forgotten container, or an unsupported internal application.

AI did not make software insecure. It always was insecure. AI just changed the economics of finding and exploiting bugs and compressed the gap between disclosure and mass exploitation from days to minutes.

Patching faster will not be enough. Critical systems need continuous inventory, automatic updates, isolation, memory-safe languages where possible. Our last bastion is software whose security can be demonstrated rather than assumed: formal verification, cryptography, memory-safe architectures, and secure hardware.

The era in which complexity provided accidental protection is ending. PHP2Shell is not an isolated crisis. It is a preview.

author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
Hermes Agent makes 3D models from text. But the real news is bigger than that.

An AI agent that makes 3D models from text? Not new.

Meshy, a text-to-3D tool, has an MCP server (a standard way to plug tools into AI agents). 

Any agent that supports MCP, including Claude and Codex, can already connect to it.

Agents asking permission before acting? 
Also not new. 

Claude Code and Codex do that all the time.

So what did Nous Research actually add with the new Meshy plugin for Hermes Agent?

The new part is the price check.

A normal approval asks: "Allow this tool?"

Hermes asks: "This costs 15 credits. Go ahead?"

In the demo, someone asks for a boss enemy for their Godot game. Hermes picks the settings (15,000 triangles, 4K textures, a GLB file for Godot), tells them the cost, and only spends after they say yes.

That's a small change, but an important one. 

Agents are starting to spend real money: credits, API calls, cloud resources. 

Permission alone isn't enough. You need to know what it costs before you click yes.

Nous also added polish on top:

→ One-line install from the official plugin catalog → Models render in the chat, and rigged characters animate there → A gallery of every model and prompt you've made → Short preview videos on messaging apps, so you can create from your phone → 3D-print prep: fixing problems, splitting into parts, handing off to a slicer

The catch: you need a Meshy Pro plan and API key, and every model costs credits.

What I find interesting as someone building agent tools: 

as agents start spending money for us, every approval should show the price, not just ask permission. 

Hermes is one of the first to make that the default.

author: brucexu_eth
quoted_text:
让 AI 帮我统计了一下自己的 Sub2API 日志，看看日常 Agent 调用里，各个模型到底有多快，以及等待时间花在哪里。

统计范围是 10 月 15 日到 22 日中午，共 40,724 条 usage 记录。这是实际工作负载，包含不同长度的上下文和输出，不是同一套题目的 benchmark。

先看 medium 档，下面是首包延迟 / 单次请求总耗时的中位数：

gpt-6-luna：0.93s / 2.70s，1,880 次
deepseek-v4.1-flash：1.95s / 4.92s，2,575 次
gpt-6.1-sol：2.23s / 7.70s，10,379 次
gpt-6-astra：2.37s / 7.93s，2,735 次

Luna 在这批记录里响应最快，但它承担了不少短输出的辅助任务，输出中位数只有 71 tokens。首包也是网关计时，不一定等于用户看到第一句正文的时间。

DeepSeek Flash 的输出吞吐比较突出，按网关计数估算的中位数约 144 tokens/s，这是真快，用的是 OpenCode 的；Sol 约 45，Astra 约 36，太慢了。

reasoning 档位的差异也值得看。Sol 的总耗时中位数：

medium 7.70s
high 13.31s
xhigh 26.52s

P90 则分别是 25.71s、83.80s、131.04s。也就是到了 xhigh，最慢的那一成请求已经超过两分钟。符合主观感受。

查错误日志还有个很实际的收获：一部分失败来自参数兼容。客户端传了 reasoning=none，实际路由到的 Sol 不支持，直接返回 400。原来 Sol 不支持关闭 reasoning 啊？

简单总结：日常交互先用 medium，需要更深推理时再开 high/xhigh；短辅助任务单独选响应快的模型。是否值得升档，还得看任务完成质量。

text:
Aerodrome and Velodrome merged to form Aero.

With this merge, the product is now live across 7 chains, including Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Robinhood Chain, increasing its addressable market by 3-4x.

To better understand this upgrade, we interviewed @wagmiAlexander, CEO of @DromosLabs, and core contributor Aero.

Aerodrome leads in bitcoin-dollar pairs and onchain FX, and is becoming a core venue for tokenised stocks too. Hence, "the intention for Aero is to continue growing across all these different assets, leveraging greater liquidity and larger market sizes to build on this success."

Aerodrome's share of tokenised-stock trading rose from around 2% in early September to ~55% by October across Ethereum and its L2s, while running only on Base.

How does Aero plan to build on this?

"New issuers will need liquidity from day one. Our model is built around a flywheel. An issuer pays incentives to attract stakers’ allocations to its market. That draws in liquidity, deeper liquidity brings in trading, and the fees captured as revenue from that trading go back to staked AERO holders, who then have a reason to keep backing the markets that perform."

Expanding to new chains means bootstrapping liquidity from scratch. On Aero, Metaswaps handle this: "a trade on one network can be filled by Aero liquidity on another, so new pools strengthen the whole network, and new deployments can draw on liquidity we already have instead of starting from nothing."

The design also keeps the growth of AI agents in mind: "We designed Aero expecting AI agents to become a meaningful part of its user base. Predictive Allocation gives them a natural role: read market data, allocate toward the markets they expect to generate revenue, and earn a share of that revenue in real time."

Additionally, the sources of revenue expand with "trading fees across seven networks, liquidity payments from issuers, expanded dynamic fees, and MEV capture on supported L2 networks through Slipstream V3."

sAERO holders receive the pool revenue, and "at today's reward targets and staking levels, the revenue it earns exceeds the dilution it absorbs."

The easiest way to compare Bittensor and Pearl is to ask: what gets you paid?

With @opentensor / $TAO, you compete to do a job well.

Each subnet sets its own tasks, such as running AI models or providing data. Miners do the work, validators score it, and those scores help determine rewards. The catch is making sure a high score means something customers actually find useful.

With @prlnet / $PRL, compatible AI calculations can also help secure a blockchain and earn mining rewards. A GPU operator could get paid for serving AI while earning PRL from the same computation.

That extra income could help lower the customer’s bill. But the subsidy depends on what those rewards are worth. And proving that computation happened doesn’t prove anyone wanted to buy its output.

For token holders, there’s another difference:

PRL is Pearl’s mining asset, while Bittensor has TAO plus separate subnet tokens called alpha. Staking into a subnet adds exposure to that subnet’s token price and liquidity.

Bittensor’s appeal is competition across many services. Pearl’s is getting more economic use from the same computation.

For both, I’d watch the same thing: PMFs

Are customers coming back and paying for the service?

text:
评测分数涨了，Agent 实际却没变好。做 Eval 最怕的就是这种「假进步」，而且它往往不是 Prompt 的问题，是 Eval 本身的问题。

Anthropic 这篇工程博客讲的就是怎么避免它，还把整套流程做成了 Claude Code 的两个命令。

① /claude-api build-eval

自动构建评估集，优先从真实任务和失败案例中选题，还会检查评分器是否稳定。同一份输出判两次，如果结果不一致，就得先检查 Eval。

② /claude-api hillclimb

让 Claude 自动改进 Prompt、Skill 或 Harness，每轮提出一项修改，再用训练集和留出测试集验证。

如果训练集分数涨了，测试集却没提升，就撤回修改，避免 Agent 只记住几个失败案例。

而且当连续优化没有效果时，它还会反过来检查 Eval 本身有没有问题，比如题目含糊、评分规则写错。

实际案例中，他们在 44 个客服工单上做优化，最终把单次成本降到了约 1/5，留出集准确率从 78.6% 提升到 90.5%。不过样本量不大，还不能直接推广。

我觉得最值得抄的是两步：评分器判两次看是否一致，以及优化卡住时让 Agent 反过来质疑 Eval。评分器自己都不稳，后面分数的涨跌就没有意义。

但有一点要注意：每轮都用测试集决定是否保留修改，测试集其实也在参与调参。如果用它跑自动 hillclimb，我会额外留一份完全没碰过的数据，在那份数据上不涨，就说明是在给测试集调参，该回滚。

做 Agent Eval、或者正在手动调 Prompt 和 Skill 的，建议先收藏。

Eugenia Kuyda, founder of @wabi, on why chatbots are the MS-DOS era of AI, and why a new interface is necessary to make AI's full potential obvious to everyone:

"It always struck me as strange that people were using products like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, but mostly for very simple use cases: for search, or to help them write something, help with homework."

"No one was really mentioning any of these exciting capabilities that we just kept seeing the models get, and so we felt like there must be an interface problem."

"There should be something simple for everyone, me included, to actually discover these amazing use cases that all these models already have."

"We got obsessed with this metaphor that the current chatbots are really the Microsoft DOS era for AI interfaces. And that there will be some sort of a Windows/MacOS moment."

text:
Kkamino, with ~$1.3B in lending TVL, has validated @chainlink CCIP as a security standard for cross-chain collateral.

Following a security review, CCIP-secured assets can qualify for higher supply caps and LTVs across Kamino markets.

The economic implications of having a security floor combined with extreme customization are significant.

Higher LTVs mean more borrowing capacity per dollar of collateral. Higher supply caps mean more capital can enter a lending market.

For tokenized asset issuers, interoperability security is now directly connected to capital efficiency and access to DeFi liquidity.

Kamino was already using Chainlink CCIP and Data Streams for its xStocks vault infrastructure. Now, CCIP's security is influencing how collateral risk is assessed.

As tokenized assets expand across chains, I expect more lending protocols to incorporate bridge security into their risk parameters.

That would give issuers another economic incentive to adopt Chainlink CCIP, beyond simply transferring assets between networks.

An “identity layer for AI agents” usually implies an entity that’s collecting data.

The owner completes a one-time passport and liveness check in the Concordium wallet.

Now we’re seeing a practical example of that with @XDCNetwork choosing Concordium as the exclusive identity verification provider for its AI marketplace.

If you’re already using agents on XDC AI, your agent can check that a verified person or business is behind the seller’s wallet before sending money, without seeing their personal details (with network fees for these registrations paid in concordium:native).

@Concordium’s Agent Registry grew from 1,131 agents in July to 4,083 in October, with verification supported across 200+ chains.

One of my top picks for playing the AI identity narrative.

New Delphi Podcast with Andrej Radonjic @0xdrej, founder of Grass

To a website, Grass looks like normal users browsing. Behind it is millions of opted in residential nodes and a data platform that has delivered exabytes of web data to the frontier labs

We get into how AI flipped the hard part of search upside down. The index used to be the moat, and crawling was free. Now AI tooling makes the index cheap, while AI crawlers have pushed the web into blocking everything. The hard part is getting the page at all

Training data is already a profitable business for Grass with most of the top labs and multiple Mag 7 companies as customers. Crawling for that data also means mapping the entire internet, which is what puts Grass in a position to build search on top of it. 从 Glassnode 10月15日 至 21日 的数据看，Bitcoin 的回升已经得到现货购买力增强的支持。主动买入金额比前一周增加4.9%，主动卖出增加1.5%，买入开始略高于卖出。同期链上实现亏损减少约32%，亏损换手也在减轻。

BTC 一周空头清算约1.58亿美元，比前周增加52%。做空仓位被迫平仓时，会产生买回需求，帮助价格继续回升。空头回补给上涨增加了另一部分买力。

从现货成交看，ETH 这一周的反弹，得到的帮助主要来自卖盘减少。主动买入金额比前周减少6.1%，主动卖出减少9.7%，卖盘缩得更多，给价格留下了回升空间。但链上实现亏损仍增加14%，接近实现盈利的两倍，整周的亏损换手状况依然偏弱。

最近三天，ETH 的承接开始改善，主动买入已超过主动卖出，链上实现亏损与盈利也接近平衡。同时，过去一周币本位期货持仓减少3.5%，空头清算增加58%，说明这次回升还伴随着仓位收缩和空头回补。

BTC 目前买入只是略高于卖出，ETH 整周买入金额仍在减少，如果卖盘重新增加、购买力跟进不足，反弹就容易再次遇到阻力。

quoted_text:
BTC 小幅上涨，合约资金开始押注反弹

从 Binance 今天下午的数据来看，BTC 和 ETH 的合约市场做多意愿有所回升，有资金在提前押注后面的上涨。价格还没有明显走高，合约持仓和多头支付的资金费已经开始增加。

截至到目前，BTC 较中午上涨约 0.4% ，合约持仓增幅也在0.4%左右。同时，BTC 下午16点结算的资金费率，从上午的0.004958%升至0.01%，ETH 则从0.003916%升至0.009885%。同样金额的多头仓位，资金费分别达到上午的约两倍和2.5倍。

个人观点来看更像是看涨资金在小幅加仓、等待反弹。持仓增加说明有新的合约仓位进入，正资金费率上升则说明做多的需求相对更强。不过新增的做多力量还没有把价格明显推上去。

后面如果买盘继续增加，这批提前加仓的多头就可能推动反弹延续。如果价格迟迟涨不动，甚至开始回落，押注上涨的资金就可能撤退，尤其是高杠杆多头，被迫平仓时反而会增加下跌压力。

目前这组数据偏向于做多情绪回暖。接下来的重点就要看美股开盘后，美国投资者的表现。

text:
这次英伟达GTC大会，着实有点无聊，没啥创新亮点，已经开始从“卖芯片”到“卖货柜”了，逐渐开始有点当年加密矿机的味道！🧐

这次大会上，黄仁勋放出了一个重磅利好：AI 数据中心从半年部署时间，现在压缩到只要 14 天。

现场发布了一个叫 DSX POD 的架构。直接把包含 Vera Rubin 芯片的整套计算设备、水冷管道、网络线缆，全都在工厂里组装测试好，塞进标准集装箱里。等货物运到现场，只要水电基础设施准备到位，插上电就能直接开干。

这场景是不是看着挺眼熟？😂

这不就是当年比特大陆 @BITMAINtech 玩剩的“蚂蚁矿箱”吗？

当年比特币挖矿争分夺秒，矿工们为了抢算力和低价电，把上百台矿机打包装进集装箱，哪里电便宜就运去哪里，落地通电即挖。今天英伟达把同样的手法用在了高端 AI 上。

虽然看似只是换了个包装，但背后却折射出两个非常关键的产业转向：

1️⃣ 芯片物理极限逼近，算力竞争转向“系统工程与模块化”

单靠微缩制程、在单块芯片上暴算力的时代越来越难走了。摩尔定律放缓，芯片迭代的边际效应越来越低。现在的竞争维度已经从“芯片怎么造”转移到了“怎么把成千上万块芯片快速搭成一个大工厂”。

模块化集装箱的本质，就是把复杂的机房建设，变成了像拼积木一样的工业流水线产品。

2️⃣ 时间就是金钱，本质上是一场“抢电抢时间”的资本游戏

黄仁勋算了一笔非常现实的账：一个 1GW 的 AI 算力工厂成本 500 亿美元，一年预期能刨出 400 亿美元收入。如果因为机房部署慢了延迟3个月，直接损失的就是 100 亿美元。

在这场资本狂飙里，设备早一天上线吐出 Token，就能早一天把真金白银收回来。

不过，英伟达的“14天奇迹”也有一个终极门槛：电力。

集装箱可以在厂里提前造好，可电网不会凭空变出来。14 天的极限部署前提，是现场已经拥有现成的电力和冷却接口。如果电网没拉通，箱子运到了也只能堆在荒郊野外吹风。

说到底，集装箱交付和“真正收钱”之间还隔着一条电力红线。AI 算力战演到今天，看似拼的是最前沿的芯片，落到实际，拼的依然是最传统的电力基建、供应链与时间成本。🧐

这里我重点依旧看好核心方向：一个是冷却龙头， $VRT ，一个是目前燃气发电龙头： $GEV 。

📝记录一下特斯拉三季报。我手里一直拿着 $TSLA，今早把财报仔细看了一遍，简单聊一聊！

先说结论：数字确实喜忧参半，但我的感受是，特斯拉正在从卖车的公司，往软件服务与AI+人形机器人方向转型。这个过程必然是痛苦的，我们需要给它一点时间。

股价来看，盘后先涨了2%，然后掉头往下。整体来说，市场第一眼看到的是惊喜，第二眼才开始慢慢算账了。🧐

📊财报，我们也来简单算个账👇

1️⃣ 营收没增长，但利润率稳住了

• 汽车收入205.6亿美金，同比降3%，不好看，但市场本来预期更差(这要感谢高油价，导致加拿大、澳洲、日本和台湾市场销售创下记录)。

• 剔除监管积分后，汽车毛利率18.1%，二季度才16.3%。

• 积分收入只有1.13亿，同比跌了73%，所以这次毛利回升不是靠卖积分堆出来的，我觉得含金量还行。

• 储能收入28.8亿，同比降16%，远低于预期的39.1亿，但毛利率冲到33%，订单和积压量还创了新高，属于交付往后挪了，利润变厚了。

• 服务收入46.1亿，同比涨33%，FSD活跃订阅超过174万，北美新车选装率破75%，软件变现这条路，也算是慢慢跑通了，期待一下全球市场的发力。

2️⃣ 自由现金流15.3亿，有点财务小把戏

市场之前预期特斯拉的自由现金流是接近-50亿，结果出来是正的，很多人欢呼。但我看了一下，三季度资本开支只有47.3亿，二季度是57.9亿，市场预期的是70多亿。

简单理解就是钱这个季度少花了，但后面得补上。如果按照预期的全年250亿的CapEx目标不变，四季度得花接近120亿。所以现金流不是变多了，是压力挪到四季度了。

3️⃣ GAAP EPS跌了44%

调整后EPS是超预期的，但GAAP直接腰斩，主要是研发和股权激励暴涨。年底前冲400MW的训练算力、奥斯汀Fab建设、Optimus在弗里蒙特试产，都在烧钱。经营现金流基本都砸进AI人形机器人的基础设施里了。

📝我的一些理解和思考：

如果还拿卖多少辆车、降价能带多少销量来衡量特斯拉，这只标的可能真没法买，营收停滞，利润腰斩。

但作为转型期的公司，我们需要换个角度思考：

• 汽车是现金奶牛，毛利守住18%左右，就能给AI训练持续输血，还能攒真实世界数据。

• FSD和Robotaxi是落地的部分，奥斯汀无监督行驶已经超过200万英里。

• Optimus是更远的一步，弗里蒙特出了首批达到量产标准的机器人，说明模型在工厂里能闭环了。

所以现在市场存在的投资分歧在于，到底我们该以15倍PE的车企给估值，还是按100倍PE的AI基建公司给估值。虽然以今天的PE来看，已经来到了355倍，整体偏贵！

最后，我最关注的一点，是特斯拉与SpaceX的合并问题。其实这个呼声，最近不断有媒体报道出来，包括马斯克自己在电话会也提到，这是一个很好的主意。

所以从马斯克的第一性原理出发，公司的边界，不应该按行业去区分，而是按算力、能源、数据来分，怎么能实现最大化效应和股东利益，来最终拍板决定。包括之前的操作案例。比如之前SolarCity并进特斯拉，X和xAI绑在一起，都是这个路子。

假如真合并了，我觉得好处还蛮多：

• 数据和GPU集群打通，车队的视频数据、星链的卫星数据、X的语言数据，一套底层AI基建通吃。

• Megapack直接按成本价供给数据中心，少一层内部交易。

• Terafab不用再走两个董事会的漫长流程，决策效率更高。

• 钛合金、一体化压铸、芯片设计这些重叠的部分，能省下一大笔重复开支。

• SpaceX的亏损还可能抵扣特斯拉的应税利润，特斯拉的现金流也能给火星计划续航。

当然，两家这么大的公司合并，反垄断和监管这关肯定不好过，而且还有一个上海工厂问题，毕竟SpaceX涉及国防承包业务，合并到一家公司，审查也有难度。

最后总结一下：卖车造血的时代放缓了，AI+人形机器人烧钱造梦的时代才刚开始。短期股价怎么波动我不太在意，我依旧会坚定持有到合并的那一天。接下来，需要关心特斯拉四季度的CapEx和FSD订阅数据增长情况，以及Optimus量产出货的情况！

以上纯属个人投资笔记，不构成建议，DYOR🙏

𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐊𝐄 𝐗 𝐍𝐀𝐍𝐒𝐄𝐍

Spoke integrates @nansen_ai  API into our Partner Intelligence feature, helping merchants review the onchain activity of potential distributors before inviting them to a campaign.

Nansen adds useful context to the partner-selection process: merchants can research a wallet directly inside Spoke and inspect the evidence behind its activity.

We use three Nansen Profiler endpoints:
1. Address Transactions: Retrieves recent activity across supported mainnet networks, including available wallet labels, networks used, transaction timestamps, and transaction evidence.
2. First Funder: Shows the earliest native-token funding returned by Nansen, with the funding address and supporting transaction.
3. Related Wallets: Provides reported wallet relationships on Monad Mainnet, including relationship types and transaction evidence.

These results appear in Spoke’s Partner Intelligence panel, accessible through distributor profiles and wallet research. Merchants can view the activity summary, expand transaction evidence, and follow explorer links to investigate further. Each lookup shows its source, retrieval time, coverage, and whether results were sampled or unavailable.

Our backend makes the authenticated Nansen requests, validates responses, and caches results for 24 hours. Fresh research is explicitly requested by the merchant and subject to credit and daily limits.
The practical value: merchants can assess potential partners using inspectable onchain evidence within the same product where they manage campaigns and invitations.

text:
Immigration policy must be driven by the present, not the past, and business leaders are too terrified of the left AND the right to acknowledge this.

Recent H1B discourse revolves around a longstanding immigration sleight-of-hand.  H1B proponents point to exceptional people who came here decades ago as if they represent the current state of the program in the same way that advocates for low-skill/illegal immigration point to very favorable immigrant crime/welfare/education/etc statistics that do, in truth, have them beating native-born Americans on many fronts.

It is all a sham.  The world that created those statistics, people, and businesses no longer exists.  Brilliant but desperate Vietnamese fathers who fled communism have nothing in common with young men from Honduras, and the crime rates/economic acccomplishments/integration of the former should not be used to justify mass migration of the latter.

Nor should the accomplishments of people who managed to get an H1B visa in the 90s (when the program was capped to just 65,000 visas) be used to justify staffing agencies and tech companies using the program to replace American jobs for less money.  The obvious abuse going on is politically suicidal and something that even the most ardent supporters of the visa should want to crack down on, no immigration program can possibly survive the obvious and widely known reality of what is going on.  I am a longtime outspoken advocate for stealing the best people from other countries to make our own better, runaway abuse of existing programs robs the government of the worker trust required to do so.

Lots of people in the tech space know this.  Even the dumb people are smart enough to see it.  Nobody actually believes these are all incredible people with unique talents performing jobs no American can.  Everyone knows the guy in Cubicle Bay 7 doing mediocre but functional web design for half the salary of his American peers is no savant and doesn't meet the statutory requirements for his H-1B visa.  

Unfortunately, most people with power or profile are terrified that any public statement or acknowledgement will get them attacked by the right (You guys have been screwing over American workers for years with visa abuse, you damn hypocrite!) or the left (You are racist, sexist, misogynist, and sucking up to this fascist administration!).  Or, more likely, both.  I know too many tech execs in particular who feel trapped, like the only winning move is to stay silent.

JD is blowing the whole thing wide open by putting facts and stats front and center that nobody wants to engage with.  Critics will talk about anything and everything else but these damning facts and this obvious truth, that H1B visas serve neither their original purpose, legal purpose, invented purpose, or the American people.

text:
It’s possible that agents will make the middlemen more powerful. An agent can find the best deal, but it still needs access to the counterparty, someone to verify delivery, and someone to bear the loss when things go wrong. Whoever controls those gates can decide which agents get access, what information they see, and whose transactions get settled. 

If that intermediary also operates its own agent, it can favor its own orders, give itself a last look, or extract fees competitors cannot avoid. 

When thousands of agents run similar decision policies, their orders may reveal the private incentives of the principals behind them. Execution gets cheaper. Control over order flow becomes more valuable. The result may be markets that look radically more open, while the power to exploit them becomes more concentrated than ever.

Sam Altman on you need self-belief to get things done:

"There's a Charlie Rose quote on this that I've always loved, and I've since added one more element to it. But the quote is that the way things get done in the world are through a combination of focus and personal connection. And the additional point I would make, after having thought about it for a while, is that the third factor is self-belief.

You really have to have a deep-seated personal conviction that this thing you're going to do that a lot of people say is really stupid is going to work and going to be important. But I think those three things, focus, personal connections, and self-belief, in my experience, are how things get done in the world."

text:
一个错误如果被 Agent 总结成 Skill，下一次它可能会更自信地再犯一遍。

《More Memory, Worse Agents》研究的就是这种 Error Reproduction。

很多 Agent Memory 会把过去轨迹总结成规则和经验，再用于后续任务。问题在于，一旦总结本身出了偏差，错误也会跟着长期保存，并继续影响之后的决策。

作者因此提出 Anti-Persistence：

真实轨迹和结果可以长期保存，但抽象出来的规则和策略只在当前任务临时生成，用完就丢。下一次再根据新的上下文重新总结。

实验覆盖 ALFWorld、WebShop 和 ScienceWorld。Anti-Persistence 在 9 个模型×任务组合里拿到 7 个最好结果，平均成功率 59.9%，同时 LLM 调用成本最低。

长期保存，并不天然等于长期学习。我的判断是：该长期存的是事实（轨迹和结果），而不是结论（规则和策略）。结论随时可以重新算，存错了却很难发现。

做 Agent Memory 或 Skill 自进化的可以先收藏。我会先检查自己的 Memory 里存的是原始轨迹还是总结出的规则；如果是规则，至少给每条记上来源轨迹，出错时能追回去。

如果某类错误在接入 Memory 之后反而更频繁了，先怀疑的就该是那几条总结出来的规则。

$102B out of $159B.

27 companies raised $1B+ rounds and absorbed roughly a 1/3 of all global funding. $100M+ rounds made up almost 90% of late-stage financing.

Frontier AI is starting to look less like normal software venture and more like heavy industry with absurd upfront costs.

Compute, datacenters, training, talent + distribution all need to be financed before anyone really knows where margins settle which is crazy. 

So we can have thousands more AI startups while the number of companies that can realistically train at the frontier keeps shrinking.

Kinda weird market structure we're in right now.

The app layer gets easier to enter while the frontier underneath it gets more capital intensive every quarter.

At this point model competition is as much a balance-sheet game as a research one.

Gensyn CEO @benfielding warns that AI agents auditing other AI agents can be compromised too:

"We create swarms of AI agents that can do far more work than any human could. A human can’t follow along and check everything. One of the big counters is to say that agents can do the verification."

"But METR says those agents themselves can become corrupted by the training process, and you can’t trust any agent that’s auditing another agent. If you’ve trained a model in an auditable way, you can trust it."

"Any claim where the model is hiding its chain of thought falls away, because you have an exact log of everything that’s happened, and you can rerun every single step on any device."

"For national security, finance, pharma, health, insurance, it’s essential that they have models like these. If a regulator wanted to audit, they wouldn’t have to go off promises of the company."

比起无人问津的内部自嗨，看到一个有讨论、有分歧、也有生命力的币安广场，绝对是好事。

text:
The word“composability” gets used to describe three very different things in blockchain, and conflating them is the source of most of the confusion around cross-chain finance.

> Bridging: An asset is locked in one place and a representation of it is created somewhere else. The asset has moved, but what you now hold is a claim on a lockbox. If the lockbox fails, the claim is worthless.

> Messaging: One chain sends a message, and another chain acts on it later. The two halves of the operation settle separately, on different schedules, under different finality rules. 

> Atomic composability: Every step of an operation, across every application and asset involved, happens in a single transaction. Either all of it succeeds, or none of it does.

TradFi knows the third one as delivery versus payment (DvP), Ethereum developers know it as atomic smart contract execution. It’s the only one that matters for finance at scale, and it’s the one Zenith was built around.

The full argument is in the article.

text:
最好的教育方式是 鼓励

我大概大三大四的时候
在学校开小吃城堕落街
那时候学校里的社团各种组织
经常来找我拉赞助

我也经常赞助这些学弟学妹
但前提都是会让他们帮我做一点小事情
比如摄影协会拉赞助
我就让他们帮我拍个视频
然后夸他们做的好
给他们一笔钱
我很少免费给他们一笔钱
让他们不劳而获

有个学妹的合作我记得很清楚
大概大四吧那时候小吃城准备开业
我为了宣传推广就公开寻求推广方案
其实我自己那时候已经写公众号了
流量在当地算不小的
在那个时候海口有1%的人口
是我的关注者
所以寻求营销方案本身就是我的营销计划
我的目的只是让别人知道 “开业”这件事
但有个学妹真的给我投了一份方案

当时这份方案并不扎眼
大部分内容其实也是我们本来计划的
我并不记得方案里的具体内容了
但是我看得出来她写的很认真
方案里的很多内容
我们应该是用到了一些
也说明她的方案也有一定的可行性
并不是完全的没有思考
虽然也都是一些常用的营销方案
但对于大一大二的学生来说已经很优秀了
方案细节我已经完全没有印象了

那个时候普通学生一个月生活费大概800-1000吧
我当时其实可以随便给他个200块钱
表示一下尊重
但我没有这样做
我给了她一笔超预期的钱
狠狠的夸了她一顿

我大概给了那个学妹1000还是2000
肯定超过她当时一个月生活费
给她钱的时候我就是有意识的
要鼓励她的思考和创业能力
让她知道她很厉害
对我来说当时这只是一笔很小的钱
但是我知道对她应该可能是第一次赚这么多
我要让她记住这种感觉

很多年过去了
她现在一年能赚几千万了
可能会有一家百亿的公司
也算事业有成了
但我相信她一定记得她第一次赚到“大钱”
记住自己很厉害的感受

海南大学
2008以下的很多学弟学妹在学校的时候
都和我合作过
也有一些在我的公司兼职过
很多人后来创业都很成功
我前前后后其实用这样的方式鼓励过很多学弟学妹
让他们感觉到
是凭借他们自己的能力
赚到“大钱”
让他们知道自己很棒很厉害

当然这不是我的功劳
因为即使这样做大部分人还是很平凡的
能成功的人还是因为自己本身的品质足够好
鼓励本身只是让这部分人觉醒
什么是觉醒
就是当你自己真的相信你很牛的时候
会赢能赢你是赢家的感觉会累积
会复利把你变成真正的牛人
“鼓励”可以把npc变成主角

我的奖学金
从来不给贫困生开特殊通道
在最穷的地方
也是你要通过成绩证明你优秀
你才可以拿钱

钱的意义是告诉他
他与众不同他很棒
而不是你弱你穷你可以得到帮助
鼓励是让一个自强自立
而扶贫只会让人更弱更穷
拿到奖学金不是因为别人施舍他
而是因为他本来就很厉害
他值得拿这笔钱

我为什么有这个理念
有两个故事：

因为我从小到大都默认自己是很牛的人
这个观念到底是从什么时候开始的
我一直写日记
有两件事情在我的日记本

第一件事是小学毕业的时候
校长来给大家发奖状三好学生
很多平时成绩都比我差的
都拿到奖学金和一本笔记本作为奖励
但所有名单都公布完了之后
却没有我的
我很难过
放学之后我跑到校长办公室问
为什么没有我的
包校长当时没有说话
我的班主任安老师笑呵呵打趣说
你那么皮三好学生不只是靠成绩的
我灰溜溜的走了
后来小学考试完了成绩公布了
我才知道我是我们小学的第一名
第一名都没有三好学生
那几年第一届五年级有了六年级
很多同学去了六年级我就直接升初中了
那会我就更委屈了
哎小学竟然是这样的方式结束的
即使考第一 
老师和校长都觉得我不配拿三好学生
这对当时的我来说打击真的很大

暑假的时候
有一天路过小学门口
就又回到之前上课的教室看看
我们小学那时候课桌板凳都是学生自己带过去的
暑假就把课桌板凳都搬走了搬回家了
教室空荡荡的
满地都是垃圾
当时虽然还小但也感受到了物是人非
有一点成长的舍离感了
我找了扫把那些把垃圾都收拾了扔了
虽然教室还是空荡荡的但是一下子干净了很多
当我依依不舍准备走出教室离开学校的时候
我才发现校长在门口站着
他轻轻和我说了一句你来下我办公室
我想了都毕业了能找我有什么就跟着他去了
他拿了一本笔记本给我
说"你现在是三好学生了"
等我回到家还发现他给我留了一段鼓励的评语
这个本子后来我用了当成日记本
但他一直保留到现在
这本滞后的三好学生奖励比我当初直接拿到要好得多
他好像真的让我理解了
什么是“三好学生”

直到今天
我都非常感激我的小学校长
更感激他给我上的最后一课
关于正确的“鼓励”的一课

第二故事是
我上初中了
语文老师要求写周记
就是每周至少要写一篇作文
写什么都可以
但我那时候好像就很能写
我几乎每天写一篇
老师是一周会把大家的收过去写个“已阅”
2003年的时候杨利伟第一次代表中国人
完成了载人航天的壮举
那天我看了小小的我感觉到莫名的激动
然后我就把那一刻的感受写到周记里了
后来在这篇周记下面
我看到了语文老师写的评语
“好小子 好好努力 前途无量”
我翻看同学们的周记
全部是千篇一律的“已阅”
只有我自己这篇周记不一样
那个时候开始我好像就真的觉得自己和别人不一样了

遇到一个好校长好老师好父母
真的会给人生超强的助攻
很多年后回头看那些行为那些文字
其实都是普普通通的
但是在那个时候
得到了校长和老师的认可
是小小心灵最大的满足
把一辈子的自信能量都充满了
如果说那时候我有多优秀
现在我三十多岁了
我觉得其实并没有
是我遇到了好校长和好老师
所以我也用这种方式去对待我能影响到的人

我们可能不会是所有人的老师校长
但我们起码是我们的孩子的启蒙老师
有时候看到孩子贪玩不做作业
或者不专注边玩边学
拖拖拉拉上课迟到又或者
说她做作业不审题
你被气哭了她也被凶得吓哭了
父母的严厉是需要的
但是鼓励是更需要的
教育的目的不是把所有的知识投喂给孩子

她不会的题现在可以来问你
她不遵守的纪律现在你可以提醒她纠正她
但是总有一天
她问的题父母也解答不了
她的纪律只能她自己来坚守

我们没有办法监督她一辈子
没有办法帮她解决她遇到的每一道题
我们只能把孩子独立思考 
自主学习的习惯养成

大学之大不在大楼而在大师
大师之大
在于引导一个人真正能自主进步的方法
这才是教育的真实目的

鼓励就是那个引导的最好办法
过度提醒等于提前责骂
而鼓励则是提前表扬
作为父母一定要多多鼓励自己的孩子

text:
Hugging Face 联合北京中关村学院、意大利科研机构，开源生物模型 Carbon-X，让研究人员可以像使用 ChatGPT 一样分析 DNA。例如，输入正常和突变后的两段 DNA，直接问「这个变化会不会致病」，模型就能给出预测和解释。它还能识别影响基因活动的区域、判断 DNA 来源，甚至补全基因序列。

Carbon-X 的底座并非最新模型，而是 2025 年发布的 Qwen3-14B。团队为它增加专门识别 DNA 的词表，将每 6 个 DNA 碱基编码为一个 Token，再用约 3020 亿 Token 的 DNA、生物学文本和指令数据继续训练，让模型既能理解基因序列，也能用自然语言回答问题。

在官方公布的 5 项 DNA 基准测试中，Carbon-X 平均得分为 66.7%，逼近 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 67.5%，超过所有参测开源模型。其中，在蛋白质编码区的突变判断和 DNA 序列补全测试中，它甚至领先所有参测模型。按照团队的算力成本估算，其单题推理成本约为 GPT-6.1 Sol API 的 1/1800。

Carbon-X 已开放模型权重，最小量化版本约 9.6GB，研究人员可以在自己的设备上处理敏感基因数据。

Project Closure Announcement

Despite our best efforts, we regret to announce that we are shutting down Zipcoin.
On October 15, we were impacted by the @UNCX_token  incident, during which a hacker drained 1.1% of the supply across the following Ethereum tokens: $pepecoin, $EDGEN, $ZC, $X, $LO0P, and $PAAL. The stolen tokens were subsequently sold on the open market. We chose to remain quiet and purchase tokens on the open market to make up for the lost future team commitments.

Shortly after lunchtime yesterday, we were alerted by @Railway that our entire codebase had been compromised. This included all secrets and private keys associated with the project. This means the attacker has access to the keys controlling project-related wallets and infrastructure, making it unsafe and unviable to continue operating. We have spent the past 12 hours trying to find a safe solution, including migrating or rotating credentials, but unfortunately, we have been unable to find a viable path forward.

We can still access the associated wallets, which hold 2.2% of the supply. We will provide all existing holders with a six-hour window to sell. At 12:00 EST, we intend to sell the remaining holdings and consolidate the funds from the associated wallets before the attacker can potentially drain them. We are deeply sorry that things have come to this. We understand the impact this will have on everyone who believed in Zipcoin's long-term potential. We genuinely believed we could build something meaningful that would contribute to the wider Ethereum ecosystem.

Unfortunately, we are only one of many teams affected. Please remain vigilant over the coming weeks.
Thank you to everyone who supported us throughout this journey. We are truly sorry that this is how it ends.

For $BTC , I'm not touching it until I see spot inflows. Without spot inflows, perps are driving the price action, making the market unstable and prone to sharp moves in both directions. Strive and others might start buying BTC after the US market opens, but there's no need to rush. Scaling in gradually is fine. There are still plenty of risks to hedge against, and even if the market moves higher, there will likely be multiple pullbacks and retests along the way.

Some altcoins are starting to show strength, mainly privacy coins, because of the PHP incident. If you want to hedge risk while avoiding FOMO, you could rotate some capital into spot positions in $XMR , $NEAR , and $ZEC , while also buying cybersecurity stocks like $CRWD , $NET , and $PANW . I've already bought some of those stocks. I'll stick to short term swings before the FOMC meeting and only deploy my full capital afterward. I'm mainly concerned about the risk of a black swan event during this period. text:
Managing DeFi positions across chains often means managing several separate systems.

You swap in one place, provide liquidity somewhere else, then work out where to vote, claim rewards, and move your capital next.

I recently covered @namidefi’s $ogNAMI presale. With its Genesis Phase approaching, here’s a closer look at how its products and economics connect ↓

1️⃣ Start with the liquidity

Nami’s three-week Genesis Phase bootstraps liquidity for its V4 DEX, which uses concentrated liquidity and dynamic fees.

You choose an eligible pool, select a price range, and deposit your tokens. While your liquidity stays active within that range, you earn Genesis Points toward launch rewards.

After Genesis, rewards become claimable from Epoch 1, with two options:

• 60% $veNAMI immediately + 40% NAMI after a two-epoch cliff, vested linearly over 90 days
• 100% $veNAMI immediately, with no vesting period

NAMI is the protocol’s native token. Locking it creates veNAMI, a voting position with access to voting rewards and trading fees.

Genesis gets liquidity into the system. What keeps the incentives working afterward?

2️⃣ d(3,3): How ongoing rewards work

Incentives can attract deposits. The harder question is how much a protocol should keep paying for them as conditions change.

Nami’s d(3,3) model adjusts emissions based on protocol performance and economic signals. Emissions can grow when sustained activity and efficiency support it, and pull back when conditions weaken.

Genesis supplies the initial activity data used to calibrate the first emission.

The aim is to make incentive spending respond to the value the protocol generates.

Regular farming emissions begin at Epoch 1. Active Farming rewards liquidity that stays active and in range, with Dual Liquidity Rewards paid by default as:

• 80% liquid NAMI.
• 20% wveNAMI, representing a permanently locked NAMI position.

LPs can choose a larger wveNAMI share when claiming, with a bonus of up to 10%.

So providing liquidity also gives users a route into deciding where future incentives go.

3️⃣ Voting across chains

wveNAMI represents Infinite veNAMI. It’s transferable, and through Nami’s interface you can use the position for voting or sell it through the marketplace.

But how does voting connect pools across different chains?

That’s where OmniLayer comes in:

• Market Layer groups related pools across chains into shared markets.
• Execution Layer uses OmniDeposit to enter and exit positions, and OmniShift to move liquidity between chains and opportunities.
• Coordination Layer uses OmniGauge to coordinate voting, rewards, and incentives across a market’s pools.

The pools still operate on their own chains, but their markets and incentives are coordinated.

You choose where to put your liquidity, and Nami handles the swaps and transfers needed to get it there.

Voting opens during Epoch 0, the final week of Genesis. You’ll need $veNAMI to participate then; Genesis rewards become claimable afterward.

4️⃣ Where does the revenue go?

Liquidity supports trading, emissions reward LPs, and voting directs incentives.

The Recursive Buyback Engine connects net protocol revenue back into that system:

• 95% buys NAMI and permanently locks it as Infinite veNAMI.
• 5% buys and burns ogNAMI.

If Nami generates $1,000 in net protocol revenue, $950 goes toward buying NAMI and $50 toward buying ogNAMI.

If you’re familiar with Hyperliquid’s revenue-funded buybacks, this is sort of like that, but with an extra loop where the locked $NAMI earns voting rewards that fund more buybacks, creating a flywheel.

The DEX’s MEV-X also captures certain arbitrage opportunities and sends the net proceeds into RBE.

So OmniLayer coordinates markets, d(3,3) adjusts emissions, and RBE feeds net revenue back through buybacks.

5️⃣ How you move through the system

Say you hold ETH and USDT across supported chains and want to provide liquidity.

OmniSwap compares and verifies quotes across swapping and bridging providers.

MultiSwap, powered by the Batcher Engine, combines multiple operations into one flow, while personal execution accounts isolate approvals from third-party providers.

OmniDeposit handles entry into your position. If opportunities change,
OmniShift coordinates the move.

As farming rewards build your voting position, Nami Relayer can automate voting, rebase, and claims for Infinite veNAMI held on Base.

Reward strategies let you receive assets such as USDC, ETH, or BTC, compound, or direct rewards into other supported Nami products as they become available.

You don’t need every tool, but they connect different parts of the same journey.

6️⃣ What else can that position do?

The NFT Marketplace lets you buy and sell Infinite veNAMI positions.

Nami Credit is designed to let you borrow $USDC against Infinite veNAMI, with voting rewards repaying the debt, no accruing interest, and no price-based liquidations. Users can also supply $USDC to its lending vault.

Credit launches once sufficient historical data is available. Its credit positions can also be traded through the marketplace.

7️⃣ Bringing it back to Genesis and ogNAMI

Genesis starts the process: active liquidity, real activity data, voting, then regular emissions.

For ogNAMI stakers, this also marks the start of USDC rewards: a share of 10% of swap fees from Nami’s eligible pools across supported chains, paid each epoch.

Alongside those rewards, RBE uses 5% of net protocol revenue to buy and burn ogNAMI.

For me, the biggest thing here is having fewer steps to manage across chains, so I’ll be watching whether that gives people a reason to stick around after Genesis.

text:
PM  @Polymarket  开始试探市场：10月底前免手续费。

利用市场的FOMO期赚取手续费，再在市场萧条的时候通过零手续费来拉人。

回头看这个赛道，这段时间 HYPE 的 HIP4 增长还是不错的，Lighter也推出了自己的预测市场，估计 PM 也感觉到了巨大的压力。

PM 成为不了 HL，并非只是手续费的问题。

PM 这个项目没有自己的精神旗帜，好像是突然起来的一个暴发户。在经历几年的埋没后，在2024年走入快车道后就失控了。这两年，他们似乎并没有清晰的路线，即使有也没能按计划去执行，社区不知道他们要去哪里，他们也很少听取社区的意见。

孤傲是很多人对当下PM的评价。

一个区块链项目成功可能有各种原因，其中必不可少的就是共识。共识就是社区的共同认知。之前，PM 是大家共识的龙头，但在今年发生这么多事情后，这种共识已经发生了很大的松动。

初始的用户圈非常重要，是共识的种子。但是，今年我看到更多的早期用户在失望中离开，或许他们还在用，但是已经没有了这种共识或者精神认可。

PM 想成为 HL, 但是急于赶路的心态让他无法静下心来学习 HL 的内在。

PM 的营销更是让人比较不舒服。你肯定见过很多推文以各种赚钱的酷炫AI工具来吸引用户，这是真的吗？真实用户的赚钱概率有多少，自己动手去参与预测一下就知道了。

更不要说，陆陆续续的各种黑料。买 KOL 用假网站来吸引用户，几年陆陆续续的宕机，一直解决不了的反复性问题，有策划的空投营销，结果不公等等。

诚然，如今PM赚到钱，但是失去了人心。

当然，赛道不眠。

PM的先发优势会随着时间而消失，今天的手续费减免或许还能暂时有效，但是明天呢？如何面对后面的新秀们？

相比PM，我更感兴趣 预测市场等期权上的进一步创新。谁的产品很酷，自然就有人去支持，支持的多了就有了核心社区。

HL和Lighter 没有花钱去经营社区，但是大家因为共识聚在一起，进而强化了共识。我们不信明星，只信身边的人的口碑。

这让我回想起第一次用 HL 和 Lighter 。只有一个感受：丝滑好用。再简单一个字形容：酷。我有动力和朋友推荐。

而如今，PM 已经不酷了。

author: tessara_ai
quoted_text:
Customers are paying billions upfront for AI capacity. And it made us wonder... what are they actually getting in return?

So we went to look it up. Our latest research note reviews disclosures from 20 AI infrastructure companies to examine what customers receive in return.

Notable examples:
- Micron: customers who meet purchase commitments get their deposits back. Pricing bands are a separate agreement.
- AXT and Coherent: a funding commitment comes with price protection and conditional refund rights.
- Core Scientific and CoreWeave: construction funding is credited against future bills, reducing later cash collections.
- Nebius: customer prepayments help fund contracted capacity, while management plans to leave some future capacity available for later sale.

one key takeaway for investors is that the company receiving the money isn’t necessarily getting the better deal. you need to model what it owes in return.
