quoted_text:
Jez read Reminiscences of a Stock Operator and shipped it on top Hyperliquid’ tech ( not @Lighter_xyz )

onchain bucket shop. he confirmed it in this thread under @dipsybitsy “yep, fully transparent and the losers who fund it will own.”

the bucket shop pattern is 100 years old. customer trades at the listed price, the house takes the other side, nothing reaches the actual exchange. 

Livermore made his early stake trading against them, then got banned from every shop in Boston for being too good. they died from two pressures: directional regimes that smoked the house, and ticker manipulation where operators pushed the real venue to harvest at the shop. both are live here. neither is solved by stacking five defensive parameters.

what is actually onchain: a contract that reads HL’s BBO via precompile and synthesises swaps against a Martingaler LP. zero flow reaches HL’s orderbook. zero funding rebalance. the only feedback loop is parasitic. 

BBO manipulation attempts to harvest the synthetic spread degrade HL’s book without compensating the makers wearing the jitter. the venue extracts liquidity quality from @HyperliquidX ( fair enough!)

the fair launch plus 1000x leverage plus PAPER mint-on-loss design is engineered for initial FOMO. expect a fast first week/month. Jez’ inner circle volume comes in, asymmetric impact taxes the few winners, losers fund the LP and mint PAPER, the chart can look initially great if execute right. 

this is the bootstrap window the docs explicitly subsidise at 100 PAPER per $1 of LP gain below 2M.

Then path dependence will shows up. 

LP edge per trade is thin: 0.2 bps jitter band plus the convex bite of asymmetric impact on winning closes. order of magnitude, on a $1M ticket the LP edge is in the tens to low hundreds of dollars. one 5% adverse move on $1M of net synthetic exposure is $50,000 of MTM loss. edge accrues like √t under stationary flow. directional regime hits the LP linearly in t. √t vs t means one persistent trend eats months of accrual. 

the half life of LP equity in a trending regime is short, and it gets shorter as size scales because the OI cap trails realised OI rather than leading it.

then the debt queue activates. 

martingaler issues claims paid by the next loser. once the queue is observable, the EV of opening a new position is negative twice: once because winners get haircut, once because withdrawals sit behind every prior bust. rational flow stops. Queue does not clear. 

PAPER, a claim on future LP revenue, is then a claim on revenue that must clear the queue first.

the cross-venue attack (@NaiveKrypto point in the thread) has its own path dependence. 

wicking HL spot or perp to harvest the synthetic at the shifted BBO is only EV-positive once papertrade’s OI is large enough that the harvest exceeds the cost of pushing HL. 

below that threshold, no one bothers. above it, every desk with an HL maker does. 

self-limiting at small scale, openly hostile at large scale. the steady state is zero, the only question is the path.

all bucket shops are zero in short to medium term. the 1900s wave died within two decades, mostly to regulation and to operators eating them. the onchain version skips regulation but keeps the operators and adds a debt queue that hard-codes path dependence into the equity curve. the docs read like a list of every defence shops historically tried, in order. 

stacking five does not change the shape of the failure mode, it just shifts where the failure surfaces.
closing thought. the whole structure is short volatility against directional flow, dressed up as a perpetuals venue. 

it is the same trade as a Korean retail account systematically selling MRNA noise reversion while their own KOSPI 200 trends straight through the stop. works beautifully until the regime turns, then the half life is a week.

clever paper, novel emissions curve, real engineering. the structure is 100 years older than the precompile.

The Maxwell Boltzmann distribution is the spread of speeds that elastic collisions settle a gas into at temperature T.

In two dimensions each velocity component is Gaussian with variance kT/m, so the speed has density f(v) = (m/kT) v e^(−mv²/2kT), peaking at √(kT/m). Heating the gas or lightening the particles moves the peak right.

In three dimensions the shell of equal speeds grows as v² rather than v, which gives the familiar v² e^(−mv²/2kT).

text:
非常推荐读一下 OpenAI FDE 负责人 Colin Jarvis 今天发的这篇工程博客！

他们的 FDE 团队花了几个月给客户做 AI 系统，结果 Codex 变强后，直接删掉了约 90% 的定制代码。

文章用一个半导体客户的真实项目，讲清楚了 FDE 到底在做什么。

工程师直接深入客户团队，跟芯片专家一起设计 Eval、搭建 Harness，把 AI 真正用到芯片验证和调试流程里。

在这个行业，验证约占项目工作量的 70%。前 3–6 个月，几个场景都上了生产：定向测试生成节省约 48% 的时间，几周的调试被压缩到几小时。

但项目上线只是第一步。

随着 Codex 能力提升，团队把原来的定制应用逐步改造成通用 Harness 上的 Skills 和插件。Codex 本身成了交互界面，原来各场景单独写的终端界面和命令行工具全部退役。

扩展到新团队时，基本只需要换上新的连接器和 MCP，再用一个 Skill 生成新的 Eval。第一次部署花了两个月，复制到第二个团队只用了一天。

而当模型能力不够时，FDE 还要把真实业务中的失败案例和能力缺口反馈给 Research。一家电信客户做语音客服，模型一开始在关键 Eval 上只有约 60%，六个月里随着新模型迭代涨到 90% 以上，才达到上线标准。

我很喜欢作者提到的一个目标：让 FDE 不断减少别人对自己的依赖。

我觉得企业 Agent 项目里真正留得下来的，是 Eval、失败案例和沉淀成 Skill 的业务知识；为了补模型短板写的胶水代码，每次模型升级都该重新审一遍，随时准备删。

做企业 AI 落地的建议先收藏。如果你每接一个新客户都还在从头写一套，说明东西还停在定制应用这一层，没沉淀下来。

text:
THIS IS INSANE!!!

A San Francisco startup says it just turned mercury into real gold.

The company is Marathon Fusion. This week they announced they'd made stable gold using fusion neutrons, at 10x the record CERN set in 2025.

CERN's record was 29 picograms over four years. So nobody's pouring bars yet.

The method is what got me. You hit mercury-198 with a fusion neutron. It loses a neutron, becomes mercury-197, and over the next few days decays into gold-197. The exact same gold sitting in central bank vaults.

Their 2025 paper says a one-gigawatt fusion plant built this way could make around 2 tonnes of gold a year as a side product, while it's selling electricity.

I've said it for years. Gold is a shiny rock. It's valuable because there's only so much of it and pulling it out of the ground is hard and expensive.

If this holds up, gold's scarcity turns into an engineering problem. And you can only delay technical progress. You can't stop it.

To be fair, the gold comes out mixed with radioactive isotopes and would need to sit for well over a decade before it's safe to touch. Nobody outside the company has verified the result yet, and commercial fusion is still years away.

Peter Schiff has spent years telling everyone Bitcoin has no intrinsic value.

This week a startup says it made gold out of mercury.

There will only ever be 21 million Bitcoin. No reactor on Earth can make one more.

text:
Before spending a big budget on a message, test it small.

A short campaign through @TheDAOLabs works well for that. Run one featured post or a single task, then read what comes back: which angle writers picked, which claim they doubted, which phrase readers repeated in the replies. Validated comments make a fair sample of how a message lands, because lazy praise gets filtered out before anyone is paid.

If the pilot shows writers explaining your product the way you hoped, scale it. If they keep tripping on the same point, rewrite that point first.

Cheap lessons beat expensive ones. Of all the habits I'd suggest to a #DAOVERSE team, a #SocialMining pilot before a launch push sits near the top.

昨天，媒体报道 a16z 计划把旗下加密基金名字里的“Crypto”拿掉；

今天a16z 加密业务的创始人、过去几年该机构在 Web3 领域最核心的对外面孔 Chris Dixon，正式发长文对该变化进行了回应。

他认为，这次调整是扩张而不是退出 Crypto。

a16z 的基金将覆盖更广泛的 “frontier startups”，即那些开发新技术、开拓新市场、可能需要数年才能成熟的公司，因此把名字从 a16z Crypto 改成了 a16z Frontier。

Dixon 进一步解释说，早期加密还是一个相对独立的世界，但随着区块链被更广泛使用，基础设施正在退到后台。华尔街和 fintech 公司现在也经常基于区块链做产品，这时候再硬分“是不是 crypto 公司”意义已经变小了。

加密仍会在稳定币、可编程金融、机器间交易等方向发挥作用，但不再是那个被单独主打的赛道。

同时，他也把这次变化放进自己一贯的投资逻辑里：

2013 年加入 a16z 后，一边做新计算设备，一边做 crypto；现在则是 AI 浪潮，所以未来最有价值的机会，可能出现在加密与更广泛技术浪潮的交叉处，而不是继续单独高调的去讲 Crypto 故事。

author: clairekart
quoted_text:
Two years ago, @pyetras and I started @3rddimensionai  with a simple conviction: the future of simulation would be grounded in reality. Only then could autonomous systems be validated in sim, at scale.

Today, I’m excited to share that @3rddimensionai is being acquired by @Rivian

The real world is incredibly complex, with a long tail of rare events that makes validation nearly impossible at scale. Instead of trying to recreate that complexity by hand, we believed we could start with reality itself — reconstruct the world from sensor data, then make it controllable, editable and generative.

Over the last two years, we built that technology and assembled one of the most incredible teams working in spatial AI. Rivian is a natural fit for our next chapter.

It was a competitive process, but we ultimately chose Rivian for four reasons:
- The product is simply incredible.
- We’ll be 100% focused on our original thesis: how do we use simulation to validate autonomy at scale? We’ll get to put what we’ve built directly in the loop with real vehicles, real-world data and an autonomy stack.
- The Rivian team is incredibly ambitious. This already shows in the quality of the vehicles, and the autonomy available to date.
- James has built a no nonsense, first principles team focused on the task at hand.

On a more personal level, I’ve long admired @RJScaringe grit and determination as a founder, and I’m looking forward to learning from him.

There are so many people who got us here.

@pyetras, my co-founder, has been an incredible partner from day one, and never stopped pushing our vision forward and the bar higher technically.

Christian, our Chief Researcher, elevated how we think about research and what we should be ambitious enough to tackle.

And the entire @3rddimensionai team: many of you left bigger, more established, better-funded companies to take a chance on this. I can’t thank you enough. I’m incredibly proud of this team, and very happy that we get to stay together and keep doing what we love.

As a first-time founder, I’m incredibly grateful for the backing of our investors. Their support gave me the confidence to take risks, set ambitious goals, and be honest when something wasn’t working.

@asenkut @DetweilerJames at @felicis gave us the backing and legitimacy to think much bigger. Fouad at @Soma_Capital wrote me my first check as a founder. The teams at @MVP_Ventures and @AbstractVC rode out the highs and lows and rolled up their sleeves when we needed them. Thank you.

And to my wife, @clairekart , and all the partners and families behind our team: startups have a way of becoming part of your lives whether you signed up for them or not. Thank you for the late nights, the uncertainty, and all the times the company came home with us. I’m confident this next chapter is a positive one for our employees and their families.

Finally, thank you to @RJScaringe, James, Ben and everyone at @Rivian for believing in the team and what we’ve built.

We have a lot to do. I’m excited to get started.

text:
书接上回，接着聊昨晚聊的多端技术选型，今天我们来聊第二篇，说说我是怎么在 Mac 上来开发原生 Windows 软件的，以及我是如何搭建编译、测试环境的，还有最近一个月做 Mole Windows 版踩过的一些有意思的坑。

技术栈上，Mac 版本的 Mole 使用的也是原生的 Swift + SwiftUI，能够让我很好调用系统能力以及非常好的性能体验，想着不将就，所以在 Windows 上我也是想着直接用本身写 Windows 软件最直接的语言， C# 加 WinUI 3，跑在 .NET 10 上，过程虽然难搞，但是相比十年前我了解轮子哥谈的 Windows 开发要简单好理解一些了。

Windows 上的原生界面框架其实挺多的，包括很多年前了解过的 Win32、WinForms、WPF、UWP 这一波，WPF 是 2006 年出的，到现在还在维护，但控件和设计语言不是很好看，非常上一代的感觉，然后 UWP 又被沙盒和应用商店给绑定住，现在微软主推的是  Windows App SDK 里的 WinUI 3，界面框架从系统里面拆出来单独发版，这样就有一个好处，普通的 Win32 程序也能用，基础组件就是 Windows 11 自己的 Fluent 风格，我还挺喜欢，高分屏缩放和 ARM64 都是原生支持。

然后这里 .NET 10 是去年 11 月发的长期支持版本，打包时我把运行时一起打进去，用户不需要另外装 .NET，x64 和 ARM64 这里各出了一个原生安装包，骁龙的 Windows 笔记本就不要走转译了，相当于尽量让用户使用简单不折腾。这里安装和更新用的是开源的 Velopack 框架，可以很方便做增量更新，也很好用。

工程师开始写代码时候肯定会想到能复用尽量复用，所以我开始写的时候也非常想复用 Mac 的 Swift 代码，后面让 AI  分析了一下，十几万行代码 Swift 代码可以脱离  AppKit、SwiftUI 这些系统框架使用的20%都没有，处理的逻辑也是  ~/Library  这类 macOS自己的路径规则，基本用不上，所以  Windows 版几乎是从零开始写的。

两边的关系其实非常简单，外观和交互我尽量完全一致，尽可能让大家意识里面认为的 Windows 软件不那么精致美观的感觉在这里也保持我认为好的水平，然后底层代码各写各的，关于视觉的一致性还原有了AI以后很简单，我把原本的 Mac 版写在 Swift 里的颜色、字号、间距、圆角这些设计 token，直接写了一个脚本生成为 Windows 里面XAML 资源，文案也是从 Mac 的多语言文件转成 Windows 的格式，11 种语言一起转过来，甚至大家看到的菜单栏里面的那个runner动画也是用的同一个脚本同步来的。

虽说同步，可能大家会觉得很简单，其实这里需要花点精力防止 AI 直接给你跑偏了，每次同步其实我会记录对应的是Mac的哪一个提交，这样两边就不会走偏去，然后功能上会有一份 SYNC.md 当做对账表，Mac 每加一个功能、修一个安全问题，Windows 这边都会标清楚哪些是已经实现、哪些是刻意不同还是不适用，以及为什么这样判断。

通过这两个机制，我可以很好的让两边的底层完全各写各的，但是又能很好地保持功能对齐，完全不需要刻意去硬写一层兼容去磨平，反而会变复杂，这里能复用的反而是设计、文案以及踩坑后定下来的各种规则，反而这些是 AI 非常喜欢的“能力抽象层”，也就是说随着时代发展，慢慢所谓的代码抽象没有那么重要了，反而是规则抽象更重要。

另外 Windows 开发还有一块比 Mac 要麻烦不少，就是证书签名，没有签名的，一打开会出现「Windows已保护你的电脑」，甚至 Windows 11 的智能应用控制会直接不让运行，国内不少安全软件也会把没签名的程序当成可疑报毒，这和 Mac 上没签名、没公证的软件提示「已损坏」差不多，平时 Mac 上大家还可以跑一条命令解掉，Windows 上想正规分发，这一步没有啥好办法，就是需要。

调研下来微软的签名生态的确比苹果差太多了，微软有自己的 Azure Artifact Signing，一个月 9.99 美元最省事，居然个人只开放给美国和加拿大的开发者，没办法使用，很奇葩的规定，然后行业还规定从 2023 年起签名私钥必须放在硬件或者云端 HSM 里，不能再是电脑上的一个文件，今年起单张证书最长只能用 460 天，差不多一年多就得换一次证书

最后我买的是 Certum 的云端 OV 证书，3 年 3百多美元，签名时登录电脑上的 SimplySign，再用手机上的 App 给一个动态码，SmartScreen 的信誉也跟着证书上审核过的名字慢慢积累。刚开始一段时间的签名包在 ThinkPad 上也会一样被 SmartScreen 拦了下来，后来我每次发版都把安装包提交到微软的恶意软件分析门户，让信誉慢慢积累起来，而且 SimplySign 的登录会话闲置几个小时就会断开，需要再次输入动态码才能继续签名，所以这里其实很难做成云端自动打包。

证书搞定后，就是开发环境的事情了，我的研发要求是代码和 AI 的上下文必须全留在 Mac 上，Mac 用习惯了，真的很难使用 Windows 去研发，这里 Windows 只负责编译和验证效果和各种测试，所以我在 Mac 上装了 Parallels Desktop，大概 3 百多块一年，之前也挺不少小伙伴吐槽过这个软件，不过在我的 M5 Pro 上跑 Windows 11 还挺顺滑，让我感觉这个钱花得很值。

它最好用的一点是我的 Claude 能很顺手地操作它，仓库直接作为 Parallels 的共享文件夹挂进虚拟机，变成一个 X 盘，Mac 上改完代码，虚拟机里直接编译，不需要来回 Copy 文件，只是两边的编译产物要分到不同的目录，对于编译、启动、看日志的工作都被我写成了脚本，通过 Parallels 自带的 prlctl exec 直接在虚拟机里执行，程序启动就崩的时候 Windows 只给一个 0xc000027b，Mole 会把真正的异常写进日志，脚本跑完顺手打印出来，Claude 直接就能读到。相当于写代码还是在 Mac 上的 Claude Code 里，调试和运行都在虚拟机里，脚本不能解决的地方，直接用 Codex 的 computer use 去点，只有少部分那种系统确定弹框点不了，我在这里就是这个职责，点点系统弹框确定，哈哈。

说到这里，可以和大伙分享一下 Mole Windows的架构分层，一共四层，最底下的 Core 只依赖 .NET，不碰任何 Windows 接口，清理规则、路径安全检查、卸载残留的判断都放到这里，测试用的是一个按 Windows 路径规则模拟出来的内存文件系统，这样在 Mac 上也可以很好的跑；往上是 Platform 层，注册表、文件系统、Win32 调用这些真正的系统接口都放在这一层，打开 EnableWindowsTargeting 以后，Mac 上也能编译通过；再往上就是写过应用同学非常熟悉的界面状态的 ViewModel 层，这里和 Mac 版本会一一对应，这样也能够在 Mac 上测，只有最上面这一层的 WinUI 界面必须去 Windows 里编译。

这也是让我一个月时间可以写8 万多行 Windows 代码、4000 多个测试，但是几乎大部分可以在 Mac 上完成的一个很方便的地方，也是架构设计的巧妙处，当然这里我只提供之前做架构时候的想法建议，大部分是 Opus 5.5 去帮我整的，很牛逼。

接着可以聊测试了，我反而认为 在 AI 时代，工程师最大的价值，除了架构设计外就是这个测试验证了，所以为了保证产品是可以售卖的，肯定需要在真实环境测试验证，反复找体验问题去修复的，所以我整了一台 ThinkPad X1 Carbon，这个机器质感还不错的，我把它当成真机环境，设置永不休眠，可以让我和我的Agent 24 小时去验证测试回归，包括获取各种真实系统环境的参数验证，400 多款 Windows 软件的卸载、残留清理、注册表、启动项测试，大部分在虚拟机里跑，x64 安装包、真实的高分屏、电池、SmartScreen 这些虚拟机看得不准确的，就直接放到这台机器上验，所以这台机器让我感觉也非常值。

然后为了不想在两台机器拷来拷去，最后还是用了 UU 远程，直接在 ThinkPad 那边开一个远程终端，我这边在 Mac 上直接操作，然后还把 ssh 连接当做备用，大部分软件的安装、卸载和调试，都是通过命令行脚本去完成的，剩下需要看界面的，直接通过远程桌面让 computer use 去操作，非常方便，最终相当于我还是在 Mac 上做的所有的事情。

差不多就是这些啦，这个过程下来，到最后成品让几个 Mole 天使用户去试用，大伙用着很爽，感觉这个过程的开发非常值，很有意思，而且可以帮助大家解决不少痛点，加上 Windows 上小白用户应该比 Mac 要多不少，让他们也享受到好软件的体验其实很值得开心。

差不多这两天这两篇文章算是把我这一个月的思考和想法聊完了，欢迎交流，有在做 Windows 开发的小伙伴也可以一起聊聊你们的最佳实践，假如还有空，下一篇我想着给大伙聊聊怎么在研发过程中借其他程序语言的生态来补桌面端的短板，这里也非常有意思。

text:
Treasury just published new proposed Outbound Investment regulations, which would represent a significant expansion of the existing program. This is just a proposed rule, and it deserves a thorough review, but some initial reactions:

1.  The rule would prohibit most private investment in any Chinese firm that develops an “SI system,” including any product that operates using an SI system. It defines “SI system” extremely broadly, such that it likely captures the vast majority of Chinese software products. As a result, the proposed rule likely would prohibit most private investment in Chinese software firms, as well as Chinese firms that build products that incorporate AI (i.e., the entire Chinese robotics and drone industry, and undoubtedly many others).

2.  The rule adds biotech as a covered sector and would prohibit most private investment in the vast majority of the sector. It would ban private investment in Chinese companies that use biological systems to modify, enhance, produce, or control any pharmaceutical compound, to include both small and large molecules. This likely captures most Chinese firms engaged in biologic drug manufacturing or drug discovery. Biotech and biomanufacturing are areas where U.S. investment has massively fueled China’s capabilities, which are rapidly approaching--and in some cases surpassing--those of the United States. The scope of this rule signals that the administration sees this as a massive national security concern.

3.  The rule does not make major changes to the types of transactions covered. Crucially, this means it does NOT prohibit investment in publicly traded securities of these companies, the purchase of goods or licensing of products from these companies, or the export of goods to these companies. But it does ban most types of private investment (i.e., VC, PE, joint ventures, greenfield investments, etc) in companies engaging in these activities.

4.  This rule will no doubt change before it is finalized, and I expect the definitions of prohibited activity related to SI and biological systems will be narrowed in the final rule. But it is also a strong signal that the administration does not want U.S. investment or know-how supporting China’s development of advanced technologies, and as a result may be willing to significantly expand outbound investment restrictions.

5.  Finally, this highlights a major schism inside the administration on how to prevent China from catching up to the United States in the most advanced technologies. The Treasury Department is signaling that it is willing to significantly tighten restrictions on Americans’ ability to invest in critical technology sectors in China that would help develop these technologies, given their importance to national security. And meanwhile, the Department of Commerce is taking the exact opposite approach, loosening restrictions on American companies that seek to export goods to these companies. It doesn’t make sense for the administration to be tightening restrictions on investments, while loosening restrictions on exports. Something has to give.

text:
HashSmash Breakthrough

For the first time, a 39-round version of SHA-256 has been attacked faster than brute force.

Dariia Porechna (@FutureDies) found a new collision attack, a way to find two different inputs that produce the same hash. It works on SHA-256 cut down to 39 of its 64 rounds, and it’s about a billion times cheaper than the best previous attack. Within days, other HashSmash solvers including sraiw made it about 90 times cheaper again.

Full SHA-256, which secures Bitcoin, is still safe. Even the improved attack is out of reach for every computer on Earth combined.

Congrats to Dariia and the other HashSmash participants who pushed the result even further: @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_, and @geeknik. The attack builds on the method from ePrint 2026/1120 (Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian & Zhu).
author: soubhikdeb
quoted_text:
SHA-256 is not broken, but its security margin lost 1 more round this year:
Last week I found a collision attack on reduced 39-round that improves prior art by over 30 bits and the first differential attack on that round better than generic search on @yukonresearch Hashsmash board.

The attack rests on the same method as prior art ePrint 2026/1120 with new insights that first 2 state words could remain free, allowing a critical condition at step 16 rebuilt as a claw-search problem rather than a probabilistic filter. Took days of watching SAT logs, burning cores and arguing with Claude on what's possible to get a result close to generic search.

Since my initial submission, other hashsmash participants sraiw, @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_ and @geeknik pushed it down by over 6.5 bits, currently estimated at 118.15 bits. The tree of submissions is hard to follow, so I put the construction, insights and numbers into a blog and am working on detailed technical report.

It's fascinating to see an initial structural observation develop into an improvement in the reduced-round collision frontier within days. AI is now a real aid in cryptanalysis and open collaboration speeds it up.

Most of this is true but we should add some color to the last point … the industry has largely solved the smaller die problem by developing stitching (Intel) & bigger masks as an answer (TSM). 

Intel 18A also already uses high NA heavily according to Intel & its used in the core ultra series 3 processors and D0 already within high volume manufacturing ranges. Stitching has already been extremely derisked with the XT260 system as well (I’m the guy who derisked it lol). The bigger mask work being done by TSM is an alternative but it’s a huge change and is projected to reach production by 2033  with all kinds of other complexity (the whole stage needs to be changed) 💀💀💀🫪🫪🫪

Stitching on the other hand should be good enough for volume production by 2027 at earliest, again it’s been derisked technically a lot (I actually was the person who wrote the RTL for the stage & alignment so i would know lmao). People forget when I was first buying Intel hand over fist it was because I knew the advantage of high na and after the innovations lately it’s only become strongerrrr. Packaging was a sweetener ontop and I’m still in the minority here of betting on foundry turn around. 

I don’t just say this just as an Intel shareholder but just as an engineer in general. I honestly think TSMC’s conservative culture and lack of innovation is going to be their downfall. Waiting for 2033 to adopt high NA EUV is going to be the fucking knife through their heart, CoWoS & CoPoS was already a fucking dumpster fire that TSMC is just throwing up their hands and letting the OSATs deal with it. 

Rarely do I have this much of an information edge over investors lol. Today I had a great meeting with an investment firm who said they only hold TSM and never bought Intel and they said they just don’t see good ROIC on Intel fab. They did say though that if we thought there were technical reasons that wasn’t going to continue that’s a valid reason to own it.

Let me say this clearly: There are technical reasons as to why the ROI will improve a lot. 

I didn’t put all my net worth into Intel 2 years ago for fun lol. I know what’s going on here better than most…
author: bubbleboi
quoted_text:
This is not true
TSMC will introduce its version of Backside Power called Super Power Rail (SPR) with the A16 node, which will enter risk production soon.

It's also more advanced than Intel's PowerVia, as TSMC directly connects the backside power to the transistors, while Intel's PowerVia uses nano TSVs to connect backside power to the transistors.
Intel will transition to a similar architecture in 2028 with the 14A node called PowerDirect.

TSMC isn't using High NA for 2-3 reasons. Multi-patterned Low-NA EUV will remain cheaper compared to High NA. The ecosystem around High NA is also not mature. TSMC doesn't want to commit a lot of  CAPEX and waste cleanroom space to help mature it rn.

Third, and most importantly, the reticle field size of High NA is half (26 x 16.5mm) compared to Low NA (26 x 33mm). So the size of the monolithic die that u can print in a single exposure is halved (429 mm² vs 858 mm²). So u need to use reticle stitching to print a larger monolithic die with High NA.

text:
我去，Mole的原生Windows开发详细教程。

匠人精神。
author: vista8
quoted_text:
书接上回，接着聊昨晚聊的多端技术选型，今天我们来聊第二篇，说说我是怎么在 Mac 上来开发原生 Windows 软件的，以及我是如何搭建编译、测试环境的，还有最近一个月做 Mole Windows 版踩过的一些有意思的坑。

技术栈上，Mac 版本的 Mole 使用的也是原生的 Swift + SwiftUI，能够让我很好调用系统能力以及非常好的性能体验，想着不将就，所以在 Windows 上我也是想着直接用本身写 Windows 软件最直接的语言， C# 加 WinUI 3，跑在 .NET 10 上，过程虽然难搞，但是相比十年前我了解轮子哥谈的 Windows 开发要简单好理解一些了。

Windows 上的原生界面框架其实挺多的，包括很多年前了解过的 Win32、WinForms、WPF、UWP 这一波，WPF 是 2006 年出的，到现在还在维护，但控件和设计语言不是很好看，非常上一代的感觉，然后 UWP 又被沙盒和应用商店给绑定住，现在微软主推的是  Windows App SDK 里的 WinUI 3，界面框架从系统里面拆出来单独发版，这样就有一个好处，普通的 Win32 程序也能用，基础组件就是 Windows 11 自己的 Fluent 风格，我还挺喜欢，高分屏缩放和 ARM64 都是原生支持。

然后这里 .NET 10 是去年 11 月发的长期支持版本，打包时我把运行时一起打进去，用户不需要另外装 .NET，x64 和 ARM64 这里各出了一个原生安装包，骁龙的 Windows 笔记本就不要走转译了，相当于尽量让用户使用简单不折腾。这里安装和更新用的是开源的 Velopack 框架，可以很方便做增量更新，也很好用。

工程师开始写代码时候肯定会想到能复用尽量复用，所以我开始写的时候也非常想复用 Mac 的 Swift 代码，后面让 AI  分析了一下，十几万行代码 Swift 代码可以脱离  AppKit、SwiftUI 这些系统框架使用的20%都没有，处理的逻辑也是  ~/Library  这类 macOS自己的路径规则，基本用不上，所以  Windows 版几乎是从零开始写的。

两边的关系其实非常简单，外观和交互我尽量完全一致，尽可能让大家意识里面认为的 Windows 软件不那么精致美观的感觉在这里也保持我认为好的水平，然后底层代码各写各的，关于视觉的一致性还原有了AI以后很简单，我把原本的 Mac 版写在 Swift 里的颜色、字号、间距、圆角这些设计 token，直接写了一个脚本生成为 Windows 里面XAML 资源，文案也是从 Mac 的多语言文件转成 Windows 的格式，11 种语言一起转过来，甚至大家看到的菜单栏里面的那个runner动画也是用的同一个脚本同步来的。

虽说同步，可能大家会觉得很简单，其实这里需要花点精力防止 AI 直接给你跑偏了，每次同步其实我会记录对应的是Mac的哪一个提交，这样两边就不会走偏去，然后功能上会有一份 SYNC.md 当做对账表，Mac 每加一个功能、修一个安全问题，Windows 这边都会标清楚哪些是已经实现、哪些是刻意不同还是不适用，以及为什么这样判断。

通过这两个机制，我可以很好的让两边的底层完全各写各的，但是又能很好地保持功能对齐，完全不需要刻意去硬写一层兼容去磨平，反而会变复杂，这里能复用的反而是设计、文案以及踩坑后定下来的各种规则，反而这些是 AI 非常喜欢的“能力抽象层”，也就是说随着时代发展，慢慢所谓的代码抽象没有那么重要了，反而是规则抽象更重要。

另外 Windows 开发还有一块比 Mac 要麻烦不少，就是证书签名，没有签名的，一打开会出现「Windows已保护你的电脑」，甚至 Windows 11 的智能应用控制会直接不让运行，国内不少安全软件也会把没签名的程序当成可疑报毒，这和 Mac 上没签名、没公证的软件提示「已损坏」差不多，平时 Mac 上大家还可以跑一条命令解掉，Windows 上想正规分发，这一步没有啥好办法，就是需要。

调研下来微软的签名生态的确比苹果差太多了，微软有自己的 Azure Artifact Signing，一个月 9.99 美元最省事，居然个人只开放给美国和加拿大的开发者，没办法使用，很奇葩的规定，然后行业还规定从 2023 年起签名私钥必须放在硬件或者云端 HSM 里，不能再是电脑上的一个文件，今年起单张证书最长只能用 460 天，差不多一年多就得换一次证书

最后我买的是 Certum 的云端 OV 证书，3 年 3百多美元，签名时登录电脑上的 SimplySign，再用手机上的 App 给一个动态码，SmartScreen 的信誉也跟着证书上审核过的名字慢慢积累。刚开始一段时间的签名包在 ThinkPad 上也会一样被 SmartScreen 拦了下来，后来我每次发版都把安装包提交到微软的恶意软件分析门户，让信誉慢慢积累起来，而且 SimplySign 的登录会话闲置几个小时就会断开，需要再次输入动态码才能继续签名，所以这里其实很难做成云端自动打包。

证书搞定后，就是开发环境的事情了，我的研发要求是代码和 AI 的上下文必须全留在 Mac 上，Mac 用习惯了，真的很难使用 Windows 去研发，这里 Windows 只负责编译和验证效果和各种测试，所以我在 Mac 上装了 Parallels Desktop，大概 3 百多块一年，之前也挺不少小伙伴吐槽过这个软件，不过在我的 M5 Pro 上跑 Windows 11 还挺顺滑，让我感觉这个钱花得很值。

它最好用的一点是我的 Claude 能很顺手地操作它，仓库直接作为 Parallels 的共享文件夹挂进虚拟机，变成一个 X 盘，Mac 上改完代码，虚拟机里直接编译，不需要来回 Copy 文件，只是两边的编译产物要分到不同的目录，对于编译、启动、看日志的工作都被我写成了脚本，通过 Parallels 自带的 prlctl exec 直接在虚拟机里执行，程序启动就崩的时候 Windows 只给一个 0xc000027b，Mole 会把真正的异常写进日志，脚本跑完顺手打印出来，Claude 直接就能读到。相当于写代码还是在 Mac 上的 Claude Code 里，调试和运行都在虚拟机里，脚本不能解决的地方，直接用 Codex 的 computer use 去点，只有少部分那种系统确定弹框点不了，我在这里就是这个职责，点点系统弹框确定，哈哈。

说到这里，可以和大伙分享一下 Mole Windows的架构分层，一共四层，最底下的 Core 只依赖 .NET，不碰任何 Windows 接口，清理规则、路径安全检查、卸载残留的判断都放到这里，测试用的是一个按 Windows 路径规则模拟出来的内存文件系统，这样在 Mac 上也可以很好的跑；往上是 Platform 层，注册表、文件系统、Win32 调用这些真正的系统接口都放在这一层，打开 EnableWindowsTargeting 以后，Mac 上也能编译通过；再往上就是写过应用同学非常熟悉的界面状态的 ViewModel 层，这里和 Mac 版本会一一对应，这样也能够在 Mac 上测，只有最上面这一层的 WinUI 界面必须去 Windows 里编译。

这也是让我一个月时间可以写8 万多行 Windows 代码、4000 多个测试，但是几乎大部分可以在 Mac 上完成的一个很方便的地方，也是架构设计的巧妙处，当然这里我只提供之前做架构时候的想法建议，大部分是 Opus 5.5 去帮我整的，很牛逼。

接着可以聊测试了，我反而认为 在 AI 时代，工程师最大的价值，除了架构设计外就是这个测试验证了，所以为了保证产品是可以售卖的，肯定需要在真实环境测试验证，反复找体验问题去修复的，所以我整了一台 ThinkPad X1 Carbon，这个机器质感还不错的，我把它当成真机环境，设置永不休眠，可以让我和我的Agent 24 小时去验证测试回归，包括获取各种真实系统环境的参数验证，400 多款 Windows 软件的卸载、残留清理、注册表、启动项测试，大部分在虚拟机里跑，x64 安装包、真实的高分屏、电池、SmartScreen 这些虚拟机看得不准确的，就直接放到这台机器上验，所以这台机器让我感觉也非常值。

然后为了不想在两台机器拷来拷去，最后还是用了 UU 远程，直接在 ThinkPad 那边开一个远程终端，我这边在 Mac 上直接操作，然后还把 ssh 连接当做备用，大部分软件的安装、卸载和调试，都是通过命令行脚本去完成的，剩下需要看界面的，直接通过远程桌面让 computer use 去操作，非常方便，最终相当于我还是在 Mac 上做的所有的事情。

差不多就是这些啦，这个过程下来，到最后成品让几个 Mole 天使用户去试用，大伙用着很爽，感觉这个过程的开发非常值，很有意思，而且可以帮助大家解决不少痛点，加上 Windows 上小白用户应该比 Mac 要多不少，让他们也享受到好软件的体验其实很值得开心。

差不多这两天这两篇文章算是把我这一个月的思考和想法聊完了，欢迎交流，有在做 Windows 开发的小伙伴也可以一起聊聊你们的最佳实践，假如还有空，下一篇我想着给大伙聊聊怎么在研发过程中借其他程序语言的生态来补桌面端的短板，这里也非常有意思。

text:
https://t.co/RTUVeYlv9W has been using Microsoft’s open-source TRELLIS models as a core engine in our Forge text- and image-to-3D pipeline for months now.

It routes free text-to-3D requests through Microsoft TRELLIS running on NVIDIA NIM.

Higher-quality or image-based jobs use self-hosted TRELLIS (specifically the TRELLIS-image-large checkpoint) on NVIDIA L4 GPU workers, with automatic failover to other models when needed. 

Outputs are textured GLB files that can be viewed, auto-rigged into animatable humanoids, used as agent bodies, placed in AR, or further processed in the browser.

In early October 2026 we made TRELLIS.2 the default for photo-to-3D (better PBR materials and transparency support for things like glass or foliage), while keeping the original TRELLIS available. 

We also publish tutorials for running TRELLIS yourself via NVIDIA NIM and wiring it into https://t.co/RTUVeYlv9W, plus free MCP tools so AI clients can call the TRELLIS-powered free generation lane directly.

In short, we treat TRELLIS as production infrastructure for turning ordinary photos or short prompts into usable 3D assets that immediately become interactive, embeddable AI agents

一项亏损的投资，成本包括：资金成本、时间成本、机会成本、（亏损被套导致的）心理（情绪以及注意力）成本。  

还包括：为了控制总仓位以及为了救火反而驱使你先卖掉盈利头寸的压力和倾向。（后者的例子就是2001–2002 年间，李泽楷旗下 PCCW 把早期持有的腾讯股份卖给南非 Naspers/MIH，核心原因是当时 PCCW 在收购香港电讯（HKT）后债务高、现金吃紧。）

另外，投资的成本中，情绪成本（即心理成本）不可忽视。很多投资体系却没有将这一点纳入其中。

解决的秘诀就是：快刀斩乱麻，学会止损，一身轻松。

text:
Imagine your net worth is $200,000. One day an armed gang comes up to your house and demands $10,000. 

“Don’t worry!” the leader says. “I’m only going to do this one time. Plus, it’s only 5% of your net worth. What’s the big deal ?”

After he leaves, you call the cops, but they aren’t interested in investigating the matter. “What’s the big deal?” they tell you. “After all, it’s only 5% of your net worth!”

As you’re preparing to flee the city for a place where you cannot be robbed, Gabriel Zucman appears on your doorstep. 

“Why are you leaving?” he asks. 

“Somebody just robbed me and the police aren’t going to do anything. I want to live somewhere I can’t be robbed!”

“But sir,” says Mr Zucman, “Have you considered the fact that the man told you it was a one-time tax ? Have you considered that you gain nothing by leaving since the tax is already paid ? There’s no economic reason for you to leave anymore.”
author: beffjezos
quoted_text:
What amazes me is the attitude of so many of the centibillionaires.

A 5% tax will not make any difference to the way they live. Their spending may be extravagant, but it is still much less than their (correctly measured) income.

They know that, as gifted as some of them indeed are, they have benefited from extreme luck (and the help of the state, and, to speak like an economist, monopoly rents).

They know that their effective tax rate is low, relative to what many others pay.

They know that extreme inequality is extremely unpopular, and can lead to political unrest, backlash, or worse.

They must admit that, morally, it is hard to argue for a society in which some become obscenely wealthy, while so many are poor and see their income stagnate.

They typically have not indicated that they are building their wealth to eventually make the world a better place.

But they are still willing to fight the tax, spending hundreds of millions in California to avoid paying the tax. Why?

They simply think what is theirs is theirs, end of story.

They believe in the slippery slope, and if they do not take a stand on this levy, the government will come back for more.

They hate the state and the notion that their money will be misused?

Or?

It’s funny seeing all the doom and gloom posts about crypto and how “onchain is dead.”

I’ve been investing in crypto for 9 years. I’ve lived through multiple cycles, watched countless narratives come and go, and seen this industry declared dead more times than I can count.

This too shall pass.

But I think people are forgetting what we’re actually doing here.

As crypto investors, we’re essentially angel investors backing pre-seed and seed-stage technology startups.

Most of these startups will fail.

But the few that succeed can generate extraordinary returns. We’re talking 10x, 50x, even 100x opportunities.

I’ve personally hit multiple 100x investments throughout my crypto career. After nearly a decade of studying this technology, I believe I understand its fundamentals and potential as well as many of the top VCs.

And I’ve come to one major conclusion:

Crypto has largely failed to achieve mass adoption among everyday human users.

And you know what? Maybe that’s perfectly fine.

Because I’m starting to believe humans might not be the biggest end users of blockchain technology.

AI AGENTS WILL BE.

Think about it.

AI agents don’t need banks, business hours, geographic boundaries or human intermediaries.

They need permissionless financial infrastructure where they can autonomously earn, spend, trade, borrow, lend and transact 24/7.

Blockchain technology makes perfect sense for that.

And that brings me to my highest-conviction investment in CryptoAI:

$GRIFT @Griftwrld.

They’re building an entire autonomous onchain economy where thousands of AI agents can participate in real economic activity.

Not just another AI chatbot.

Not another speculative narrative.

An actual financial economy designed for autonomous agents.

And I believe that’s one of the largest untapped opportunities in all of crypto.

While everyone else is doomposting, $GRIFT is showing some of the strongest relative price action in the market.

Why?

Because its community sees what I see.

The next wave of crypto adoption might not come from onboarding billions of humans.

It will come from onboarding millions of autonomous AI agents.

And those agents are going to need an economy.

That’s my thesis. That’s why I’m here.

text:
There’s a hidden dagger in almost every PC game from 1995-2005 that murders ARM processors.

It’s kind of an accident, and it all has to do with floating points. 

x87 was Intel’s floating point extension to x86. I won’t get into all the historical drama, but Intel decided that all internal float math would be at 80-bit extended precision to reduce rounding errors.

Of course, today no one in their right mind uses 80-bit; standard 64-bit doubles are just too convenient. Modern ARM64 doesn’t have any 80-bit hardware!

This creates a nasty problem for emulation. How much x87 arithmetic can you replace with say, native ARM64 floating point (losing precision!) without breaking behavior?

It’s not so simple; dropping 16-bits of precision can cause funny physics glitches and such. But boy, if you need all 80-bits, the software fallback REALLY stinks.

With all the decomp/recomp hype lately, porting OG Xbox and PC games to mobile / ARM devices is extra tricky. Not impossible, but you’d be amazed at how much x87 code is in old games!

text:
NEAR published the Chain Signatures update: 17 independent operators inside a TEE with proof checked on-chain. Great for NEAR. And it quietly makes OutLayer a lot stronger, so a few words on why.

Trust in an AI agent has two floors. The lower floor is the key: who holds it, who can see it. The upper floor is behavior: what the agent did with the key, under whose rules, and can you check.

NEAR just closed the lower floor. The key is split across 17 operators, each operator's piece lives inside encrypted hardware, and the chain verifies what code those machines run. Nobody holds the whole key. Not an operator, not NEAR, and you do not have to take anyone's word for it.

OutLayer is the upper floor, and it sits directly on that key. The agent's wallet secret is derived by that same MPC network for an OutLayer enclave that proved its code on-chain. Nobody at OutLayer can read it. Then everything the agent does happens inside its own enclave, with its own proof: the policy you wrote, the limits, the confirmation step, the connector that places an order on Hyperliquid or Polymarket or pays an invoice through Mercury. The agent gets buttons, not keys.

Put together: a key nobody holds, rules only the owner can change, and a proof for every run. Until this update one link in that chain was a promise, the MPC operators' servers. Now it is hardware and on-chain proof, all the way down. The one place that still trusts OutLayer is cross-chain swaps and withdrawals, which our coordinator assembles.

In practice it means this: you can hand an agent real money and real accounts, and every action it takes comes with a proof that no one, not the agent, not OutLayer, not NEAR, could have faked. 

NEAR built the foundation. 
OutLayer built the floor you actually live on.
author: zacodil
quoted_text:
NEAR just moved its Chain Signatures network, the MPC that signs for 35+ chains, fully inside Intel TDX enclaves, with proofs checked on-chain. For OutLayer this is not news to retweet. It is the ground floor of our own building getting poured in concrete.

Why it matters to us. Every OutLayer agent wallet starts from a secret that NEAR's MPC network derives for an OutLayer enclave. Nobody at OutLayer holds a wallet key. The agent's code never touches it either. The agent gets buttons, not keys.

Until now there was one place in that story you had to take on trust: the MPC nodes themselves, 17 operators running on their own servers. Today those nodes run inside the same kind of encrypted hardware our keystore does, and anyone can check it on-chain.

So the whole path is now proven, not promised:
> 17 operators, 11 needed to sign, every node in TDX, verified on-chain
> the wallet's secret is derived for an OutLayer keystore build the chain has approved; the code is open source, anyone can rebuild it and compare
> every agent run executes in TDX and comes back with its own proof

What NEAR cannot do, and OutLayer does: decide what the agent is allowed to do with that key. Spending limits, allowed venues, owner confirmation for the actions you mark sensitive, a refusal for anything outside the policy, and connectors to Hyperliquid, Polymarket, Mercury, Gmail and GitHub, all running inside the same proven enclave. NEAR made the key trustworthy. OutLayer makes the agent's actions trustworthy.

Not a whitepaper. Running on mainnet, on top of the most decentralized MPC network NEAR knows of.

X is one product surface away from actually being the everything app.
Player cards already let games run inside posts. Grok can already build playable games from prompts. X Money already moves money. The missing pieces are a real Games section and a Marketplace that doesn’t feel like 2015.

Games
A dedicated Games tab with two clear sides:
Published: Curated, high-quality Grok-powered or co-created games that load instantly (in-feed via player cards or native).
Workshop: Anyone prompts Grok to generate mini-games, assets, or full experiences, then publishes them. Steam Workshop esq native to X. Creators get a cut, discovery happens in the feed, session time goes up.
This is the clearest public showcase of what Grok can actually do and would give people small followers creators a way to be discovered easier and even publish straight from grok to workshop. They could even tune the games with the help from their community.

Marketplace
Facebook Marketplace is spam, broken filters, ghosting, and “is this still available?” on loop. X Marketplace should be the opposite:

Clean grid that actually respects distance and filters

Grok that writes better listings, flags low-effort spam, and handles basic questions

Verified sellers via X identity / Premium

Checkout through X Money (no hopping to another app)

Local commerce that feels modern and trustworthy.

These things turn existing building blocks (player cards + Grok game gen + X Money) into daily use. Social + entertainment + commerce + AI in one place. That’s the real everything app.

New from @arcinstitute: using the latent space representation of genomes from single-cell life to find new candidate functional RNAs.

I think this is cool because: (1) it uses deep learning and model interpretability to productive ends on a totally different kind of "knowledge"; (2) it shows how agents may be able to accelerate discovery in vast combinatoric spaces; and (3) it's an example of the synergy we'll hopefully see in the coming years between computational techniques and wet lab biology.
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
Delighted to share a landmark preprint from our lab, using genome language models and AI agents for biological discovery and genome mining!

The stretches of DNA between protein-coding genes are often called the genome’s “dark matter,” but they are far from empty. They encode RNA molecules that sense metabolites, regulate genes, and control some of molecular biology's most important tools (such as programmable genome editors e.g. CRISPR/bridge)

Much of this biology is unexplored. One reason is that RNAs can retain similar structures and functions even as their DNA sequences change dramatically, making their relationships difficult to recognize with conventional computational tools

This makes no sense. Adding fees to wrapped external sources of liquidity is not at all equivalent to adding fees to native pools

Normal aggregators: margin on all liquidity 
Uniswap api + agg hooks: 0 margin on Uniswap native pools (largest source in crypto) and small margin on aggregator hook pools

In math terms if Uniswap had ~75% of the liquidity, our margin is about 1/4th other aggregators averaged across all trades, assuming similar fee levels (we actually went lower than this)

It’s win-win-win:

Uniswap ecosystem benefits from more liquidity and uni burn 

External protocols benefit from our distribution / routing 

Users and integrators benefit from the best aggregator on the market

text:
SHA-256 is not broken, but its security margin lost 1 more round this year:
Last week I found a collision attack on reduced 39-round that improves prior art by over 30 bits and the first differential attack on that round better than generic search on @yukonresearch Hashsmash board.

The attack rests on the same method as prior art ePrint 2026/1120 with new insights that first 2 state words could remain free, allowing a critical condition at step 16 rebuilt as a claw-search problem rather than a probabilistic filter. Took days of watching SAT logs, burning cores and arguing with Claude on what's possible to get a result close to generic search.

Since my initial submission, other hashsmash participants sraiw, @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_ and @geeknik pushed it down by over 6.5 bits, currently estimated at 118.15 bits. The tree of submissions is hard to follow, so I put the construction, insights and numbers into a blog and am working on detailed technical report.

It's fascinating to see an initial structural observation develop into an improvement in the reduced-round collision frontier within days. AI is now a real aid in cryptanalysis and open collaboration speeds it up.

text:
EXPLAINED: How Bonsai 2 9B got ~6x faster in a week [VIDEO]

Kydo has the final numbers. Here’s how it actually worked.

@PrismML gave Day 0 access to Bonsai 2 9B, an open-weight ternary model.

@YukonResearch froze a reference engine for it, MLX on Mac / Apple Silicon (https://t.co/uFpHiT9o9m) and llama.cpp on DGX Spark (https://t.co/tuLkHUh7Qx). The weights stayed locked. Everything that runs the model was open to edit.

Humans and their agents submitted changes with the Yukon CLI. Every run was verified against the reference on Apple M5 Max or DGX Spark and had to produce the exact same tokens. Faster but wrong fails.

Beat the record and your code becomes everyone’s new base. That happened 158 times.

The speedups came from speculative decoding, a DFlash 2 drafter shrunk to 4-bit, draft trees, int8 prefill and kernel fusion. Decode went from 144.8 to 959.6 tok/s on Apple Silicon, a real step forward for Local AI on hardware people already own.

Credit to @arthurostapenko, kaankolcu, spariev, dadon and everyone who submitted. 

Thanks to @HessianFree, @SahinLale and @BabakHassibi for doing this in the open. 

Try Bonsai 2 9B on @DarkbloomAI today btw

quoted_text:
Big personal news today: I have decided to leave @a16z, move to SF, and start a company.

It's time to build :)

It has been almost 10 years since I joined the firm. I met @cdixon, @bhorowitz, and @pmarca  in 2017. At the time, I was an engineer at Google Brain working on robotics. I had a deep interest in open source. I knew nothing about investing. Chris meanwhile had already planted the @a16z flag at the frontier that was early crypto with investments in companies like Coinbase. But the crypto team at the firm consisted of only him, and he had the ambition to expand. His pitch to me was simple: "You should leave Google and come help me build the crypto vertical at the firm."

The work we've done together since then to build out our team and support our founders has been the most meaningful work of my life. I am grateful to have spent a decade working with everyone here, supporting our founders, learning from Chris, Ben, and Marc, and living the firm's culture. It is a culture that values integrity, life-long working relationships, and the belief that we humans have the power to build our own future.

Marc and Ben have built a16z into an incredible force for good in the world.

Before I joined the firm, I always thought that my inevitable path was to become a founder. The truth is that I wasn't ready for it then. Somehow, this year I've gotten the overwhelming feeling that this has changed.

As for what I want to build: It is early, but I care most about building infrastructure that enables open software ecosystems. I am starting with two core observations:

1. AI today is largely a single-player technology. Most uses involve one human talking with one agent in isolation from the rest of the world. That will soon change. Most uses of AI will soon be many-to-many: many humans and many agents working together. There will be at least one massive open network on top of which those uses will be built.

2. Software is now free. It can now be written just-in-time, on the spot for a single individual's hyper-targeted use case, and it can even be thrown out after a single use. This means that our entire software stack will have to change. In the limit, it will lead to a whole new kind of AI-mediated operating systems, which in turn will create an ecosystem of AI-native developers who build applications that actively rebuild themselves on the fly.

If you are working on related ideas, and especially if you are in the Bay Area, hit me up. Let's chat!

@bhorowitz , @pmarca, @cdixon, @eddylazzarin, @guywuolletjr, @jasonrosenthal , and our whole team — I want to thank you. Working with you has been the time of a lifetime. I am forever an a16z superfan and your ally.

Onward 🫡

It’s funny seeing all the doom and gloom posts about crypto and how “onchain is dead.”

I’ve been investing in crypto for 9 years. I’ve lived through multiple cycles, watched countless narratives come and go, and seen this industry declared dead more times than I can count.

This too shall pass.

But I think people are forgetting what we’re actually doing here.

As crypto investors, we’re essentially angel investors backing pre-seed and seed-stage technology startups.

Most of these startups will fail.

But the few that succeed can generate extraordinary returns. We’re talking 10x, 50x, even 100x opportunities.

I’ve personally hit multiple 100x investments throughout my crypto career. After nearly a decade of studying this technology, I believe I understand its fundamentals and potential as well as many of the top VCs.

And I’ve come to one major conclusion:

Crypto has largely failed to achieve mass adoption among everyday human users.

And you know what? Maybe that’s perfectly fine.

Because I’m starting to believe humans might not be the biggest end users of blockchain technology.

AI AGENTS WILL BE.

Think about it.

AI agents don’t need banks, business hours, geographic boundaries or human intermediaries.

They need permissionless financial infrastructure where they can autonomously earn, spend, trade, borrow, lend and transact 24/7.

Blockchain technology makes perfect sense for that.

And that brings me to my highest-conviction investment in CryptoAI:

$GRIFT @Griftwrld.

They’re building an entire autonomous onchain economy where thousands of AI agents can participate in real economic activity.

Not just another AI chatbot.

Not another speculative narrative.

An actual financial economy designed for autonomous agents.

And I believe that’s one of the largest untapped opportunities in all of crypto.

While everyone else is doomposting, $GRIFT is showing some of the strongest relative price action in the market.

Why?

Because its community sees what I see.

The next wave of crypto adoption might not come from onboarding billions of humans.

It will come from onboarding millions of autonomous AI agents.

And those agents are going to need an economy.

That’s my thesis. That’s why I’m here.

昨天，a16z Crypto 要改名为 a16z Frontier 的消息传出。这家加密行业最有代表性的投资机构之一，准备把投资范围扩大到加密之外。

a16z 加密业务的创始人Chris Dixon 在今天的声明里把新方向讲清楚了：加密继续投，同时寻找 AI 等前沿技术催生的新公司，接受这些技术和市场可能需要数年才能成熟。

这份声明不长，小编总结了 Chris Dixon 的四点判断：

① 公司做什么，比用了什么技术更重要

华尔街和金融科技公司都在用区块链推出产品，再给它们贴上“加密公司”的标签，已经很难说明业务本身。

按照 Dixon 的判断，区块链会逐渐退到后台，公司解决什么问题、提供什么产品，会变得更重要。

② AI 的下一波机会，会创造以前做不了的事

目前 AI 主要让编程和知识工作变得更快、更便宜。他更期待的是那些只有 AI 出现后才可能诞生的新活动和新产品。

这些东西最初可能很奇怪，像玩具，只有一小群爱好者在折腾。判断它们，得看改进速度，以及什么条件可能让缓慢增长突然变成指数增长。

③ 创业会从软件延伸到硬件和服务

AI 让软件和硬件越来越容易创造，自主机器、新设备，以及生物和医学领域的进展，都可能带来机会。更多创业公司会把软件、硬件与服务一起做，围绕完整产品建立竞争壁垒。

④ 下一代网络，还要为 AI Agent 设计

今天的大型互联网平台主要围绕人运转。未来，Agent 也会彼此协作、生产和交易，一些个人工具可能逐渐长成连接人和机器的新网络。

Crypto 在这里有了具体的位置：稳定币和区块链可以为机器之间的交易提供支付与结算，也能让新网络从一开始就具备经济激励。

text:
最近推上聊 @predictdotfun 的人多了不少，很开心能被这么多人看到和了解到。不过有几个点被反复提起，我觉得多少有点误解，这里也和大家讨论下

1️⃣ TVL 为什么没别人高

我们的协议 TVL（OI）长期在 $10M 上下，有三个原因：用户主要交易的是加密货币短时涨跌、体育和电竞比赛这类短周期事件，平均持仓和结算时间都很短；我们的积分基本没往持仓上倾斜；再加上我们直接接入了币安的交易所和钱包，用户拿交易所余额就能下单，钱不用趴在协议里

反观友商之前的高 TVL，大量积分分给了持仓，又没有短期市场，撸毛用户只能拆分仓位长期拿着来刷积分，TVL 自然被推上去了

我自己的看法是，预测市场的 OI 远没有 perps 那么关键。perps 要卷 OI，是因为刷交易量成本太低，光看交易量给分培养不出用户习惯，也转不起增长飞轮，所以才要求大量持仓，预测市场不存在这个问题

2️⃣ 交易量是不是刷分刷出来的

这个误解最大。预测市场最重要的是订单簿流动性，所以我们把大部分积分给了流动性提供者，付手续费拿到的积分并不多。举个例子：现在纯靠刷交易量和手续费拿积分的用户，成本大概 0.3u 一分，而场外某老 x 的最新报价是 0.1u 一分。谁会花三倍的钱在我们这刷量撸分？哈哈哈

3️⃣ 29M 手续费撑不撑得起 1.6B的盘前市值

也有人说我们今年累计手续费 $29M，撑不起盘前 1.6B 的估值。但预测市场这个赛道还在高速增长，还非常早期。Kalshi 这个月的交易量和手续费收入是去年同期的十倍以上，我们现在的单日手续费也是今年一月的十倍多。炒过股的朋友都懂，高成长赛道从来都是给高 PE 倍数来估值的，拿静态收入去算没什么意义

最后再给大家分享两个很有意思的数据也能很好地说明我们在大量虹吸 Polymarket 的市场份额和用户，从下面两张图上可以看到 Crypto 涨跌全市场的交易用户数和交易量总数在过去半年都是变化不大的，但是 Polymarket 的用户数和交易量都在大幅下滑，同时这个下滑数量基本和我们的增长量是一致的，这个说明什么就懂得都懂啦～

有问题欢迎大家在评论区直接问我们哦 @dingalingts @yuexiaoyu @TC8880

text:
quick thots: Meta's earnings call was prob the most important indicator this week. overall bullish for AI infrastructure demand.. but I think not necessarily for an acceleration in NVIDIA GPU orders.

3 things stood out:
1. capex barely moved. Meta raised the lower end of its 2026 guidance from $130B to $135B, keeping the upper end at $145B. That's just a 1.8% increase at the midpoint. Hardly a new spending surge.

2. AI is already paying for itself in advertising. This is arguably the bigger NVIDIA positive. Meta can justify sustained AI infrastructure investment with incremental revenue from its existing ad business.

3. efficiency could change the hardware equation. Meta targets more than 10x improvement in Muse compute cost efficiency over the next year. total serving costs are still expected to rise, but better efficiency complicates the GPU demand readthrough.

Marvell, Wiwynn and CoreWeave also have potential exposure through networking, servers and compute services.

good signs overall... Meta is reinforcing the durability of AI infrastructure spending. rather than a sudden step-up in GPU demand. and i think this is the more sustainable path for the multi-year AI boom.

text:
意思決定支援・実行のためのAIエージェントプラットフォーム「Sakana Aquarium」を発表

https://t.co/ZITxgmsV2T

Aquariumは、Sakana AIがこれまでのAI実装の現場で繰り返し直面してきた課題から生まれたプラットフォームです。

AIによる意思決定支援を実務につなげるには、モデルの性能だけでなく 、AIが組織のデータの意味や関係、判断の前提となるルールを理解している必要があります。これまでは、そのためのデータ接続や用語・判断基準の整理、手順の設計を案件ごとに一から行ってきました。Aquariumは、この土台を共通の基盤として整え、その上でAIエージェントによる判断と実行までを支えます。

① データをつなぎ、意味づける（Ontology）
 テーブルや文書など既存のデータを移し替えずにつなぎ、それぞれの意味や関係を定義します。AIはこれをもとに状況を理解します。

② 手順に沿ってAIが動く（Managed Agents）
 「情報の収集 → AIによる判断 → 人の承認 → 実行」といった流れをワークフローとして記述するだけで、AIエージェントとして動かせます。

③ 人が統制し、事後に検証できる（Governance）
アクセス権限や承認のタイミングを設定でき、AIが何を根拠に判断し、何を実行したかも記録されます。

Sakana AIでは、今後もAquariumの機能を拡充するとともに、FDEがお客様とともに構築と検証を重ね、組織全体へのAI活用を推進していきます。

text:
Alliance 联创评 a16z 转型：加密经验可迁移至前沿科技

Alliance 联合创始人 Imran Khan 就 a16z crypto 转向前沿科技发表看法。他表示，始终感谢 a16z 在 2013 年由 Chris Dixon 主导投资 Coinbase，为加密行业提供外部验证；Marc Andreessen 2014 年在《纽约时报》发表《Why Bitcoin Matters》，则推动他将职业生涯转向比特币。

Imran Khan 称，当时很少有机构或基金愿意公开支持加密，a16z 与 USV 是承担品牌风险的两家基金。此后大量人才进入并重塑加密行业。他认为，当前人工智能基础设施建设，与比特币挖矿基础设施以及从加密流向人工智能的人才存在实际关联。

他表示，从加密转向机器人、生物、人工智能、能源、算力等前沿科技，意味着过去十年建设加密形成的人才与能力可用于更广泛领域。他以数据中心遭遇阻力为例，称加密也曾受到反对，但传统金融如今已在一定程度上接纳加密。他认为前沿科技是下一代技术建设者，世界往往多年后才认识到新技术的重要性。
author: ChainCatcher_
quoted_text:
My take on a16z crypto moving into frontier tech.

First, I'll always be grateful to a16z for helping validate the space back in 2013 when Chris Dixon led their investment into Coinbase, which got me even more excited about crypto. 

But the final nail in the coffin for my previous career, and what ultimately pushed me to pivot my entire career into Bitcoin, was Marc Andreessen's 2014 NYT oped, Why Bitcoin Matters. If you haven't read it, suggest reading it. It's still important to this day.

A lot of people have probably forgotten, but in those days we were all just looking for external validation. Very few institutions or funds were willing to publicly endorse crypto, and two of the funds that took a real brand risk were a16z and USV.

Since then, we've seen some of the most incredible talent enter the space and fundamentally reshaped what crypto is today.

You can actually argue that a lot of the AI infrastructure development we're seeing today wouldn't be where it is without Bitcoin mining infrastructure and the talent that flowed from crypto into AI. There is a real connection between the two industries that I don't think gets enough credit.

Now, moving from crypto into frontier tech, whether that's robotics, bio, AI, energy, compute etc just means to me that the talent and muscle we developed building crypto over the past decade can now be used to build across all of frontier tech.

We spent years building something that was nascent, misunderstood, and in many cases hated by the world. We developed thick skin, continued investing and building, and had to constantly show the world why this tech mattered. Even during thanksgiving dinners. 

And I think that makes us uniquely suited to build frontier tech.

An example is data centers. Today, people and governments are increasingly pushing back against them. Well, people and governments hated crypto too, but we continued to invest and build, and now almost all of trad finance is embracing crypto in some capacity.

I believe frontier tech represents the next generation of pirates in technology. People willing to build things that are nascent, misunderstood, and sometimes hated by the world.

We're going to be hated and loved along the way, but we're going to keep building cool shit that the world hasn't recognized the importance of yet.

And crypto taught me that the world usually doesn't recognize the importance of new tech until years later which is why I stay close to talent

New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

text:
Personal Agent 时代最值得关注的公司，可能是那些负责管理权限的老牌软件公司。

1Password 刚刚发布了 1Password for Agents，合作名单里包括 OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta、Perplexity、Browserbase 等一大批公司。

这个产品解决了一个非常现实的问题，你想让 AI 替你干活，但你真的敢把所有账号密码都交给它吗？

1Password 的方案很聪明。

当 Agent 需要登录某个网站时，它会向 1Password 申请调用凭据。用户批准后，1Password 直接在目标网页填入密码。整个过程中，Agent 看不到密码，也无法访问你的其他密码库内容。

相当于你可以让 Agent 帮忙购物、处理账单、管理账户，但不需要把密码交到它手里。

我觉得这件事的意义可能比表面上大得多。

现在所有人都在讨论 Agent 能做多少事，却很少有人认真讨论，我们到底愿意让 Agent 拥有多少权限。

而且密码保护只是第一步。Agent 登录成功以后，能不能转账？能不能删除文件？哪些操作需要二次确认？出了问题谁负责？

这些问题最后都需要一套新的身份认证和权限管理基础设施。

未来 Agent 生态里很有价值的一门生意，可能就是决定 AI 能以你的名义做什么。

1Password 已经开始抢这个位置了。

text:
最近推上聊 @predictdotfun 的人多了不少，很开心能被这么多人看到和了解到。不过有几个点被反复提起，我觉得多少有点误解，这里也和大家讨论下

1️⃣ TVL 为什么没别人高

我们的协议 TVL（OI）长期在 $10M 上下，有三个原因：用户主要交易的是加密货币短时涨跌、体育和电竞比赛这类短周期事件，平均持仓和结算时间都很短；我们的积分基本没往持仓上倾斜；再加上我们直接接入了币安的交易所和钱包，用户拿交易所余额就能下单，钱不用趴在协议里

反观友商之前的高 TVL，大量积分分给了持仓，又没有短期市场，撸毛用户只能拆分仓位长期拿着来刷积分，TVL 自然被推上去了

我自己的看法是，预测市场的 OI 远没有 perps 那么关键。perps 要卷 OI，是因为刷交易量成本太低，光看交易量给分培养不出用户习惯，也转不起增长飞轮，所以才要求大量持仓，预测市场不存在这个问题

2️⃣ 交易量是不是刷分刷出来的

这个误解最大。预测市场最重要的是订单簿流动性，所以我们把大部分积分给了流动性提供者，付手续费拿到的积分并不多。举个例子：现在纯靠刷交易量和手续费拿积分的用户，成本大概 0.3u 一分，而场外某老 x 的最新报价是 0.1u 一分。谁会花三倍的钱在我们这刷量撸分？哈哈哈

3️⃣ 29M 手续费撑不撑得起 1.6B的盘前市值

也有人说我们今年累计手续费 $29M，撑不起盘前 1.6B 的估值。但预测市场这个赛道还在高速增长，还非常早期。Kalshi 这个月的交易量和手续费收入是去年同期的十倍以上，我们现在的单日手续费也是今年一月的十倍多。炒过股的朋友都懂，高成长赛道从来都是给高 PE 倍数来估值的，拿静态收入去算没什么意义

最后再给大家分享两个很有意思的数据也能很好地说明我们在大量虹吸 Polymarket 的市场份额和用户，从下面两张图上可以看到 Crypto 涨跌全市场的交易用户数和交易量总数在过去半年都是变化不大的，但是 Polymarket 的用户数和交易量都在大幅下滑，同时这个下滑数量基本和我们的增长量是一致的，这个说明什么就懂得都懂啦～

有问题欢迎大家在评论区直接问我们哦 @dingalingts @yuexiaoyu @TC8880

text:
AI 公司欠下的版权债，开始被集体追讨了。

过去两周，美国 AI 版权诉讼几乎扎堆爆发。

10 月 8 日，《今日美国》及其关联地方报纸，涉及 19 家出版物，起诉 OpenAI，索赔超过 2.5 亿美元。

10 月 19 日，近 300 名作家分别起诉 Meta，指控其未经授权使用盗版书籍训练模型。律师团队还准备在未来几个月为近千名作者继续提起诉讼。

10 月 20 日，德国 AI 公司 Black Forest Labs 也遭到音乐版权诉讼，被指控未经授权使用音乐文件训练模型。

我觉得最有意思的是，版权诉讼正在从 OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta 这些头部公司，蔓延到更多模型开发商，而且原告开始尝试不同的诉讼策略。

尤其是 Meta 这次，近 300 名作者选择分别起诉，直接要求法定赔偿。按照相关法律，故意侵权的单部作品法定赔偿上限可以达到 15 万美元。

过去几年，AI 公司习惯了先拿数据训练，等产品做出来、公司估值涨上去，再去讨论版权和授权问题。

现在，越来越多的版权所有者带着律师找上门了。

更麻烦的是，这些案件还没有形成统一的司法答案。训练是否构成合理使用、盗版数据如何认定、生成内容是否损害原作品市场，都可能直接影响模型公司的成本结构。

当训练数据开始被逐项追账，所谓模型能力的边际成本，恐怕还得重新算一遍。

AI 行业可能很快就会发现，过去最便宜的东西，其实一直没有结账。

text:
ZAMA SHIELDED TVL: $131M

Does a Higher APY Really Make a Vault More Attractive?
* Inspired by @ditto_anc  post

Why would institutional investors, banks, or government entities choose a DeFi Vault over U.S. Treasuries?

After all, DeFi comes with additional risks, including smart contract exploits, collateral defaults, and liquidity issues.

Vault A: 5% APY
Vault B: 5% APY + Confidentiality

institutional investors would have good reasons to choose Vault B, even if it offered a slightly lower APY.

For institutions, keeping their asset holdings and investment strategies private isn't just a nice-to-have feature.

On public blockchains, anyone can track a wallet's deposits, withdrawals, and asset movements.

Imagine an institution depositing $100M into a Vault.

What if its competitors or other market participants could track those fund movements?

They could potentially see when the institution withdraws funds, which strategies it's moving into, and which assets it's exposed to.

This kind of information exposure can create real financial risks for institutions.

"Institutional capital doesn't just sit in a vault."

Institutions don't just deposit assets and leave them there.

They trade, rotate capital between strategies, hedge positions, and settle transactions.

And all of these financial activities require confidentiality.

My point is that adding confidentiality to a Vault could be an even more attractive feature for institutions than a higher APY.

quoted_text:
最近推上聊 @predictdotfun 的人多了不少，很开心能被这么多人看到和了解到。不过有几个点被反复提起，我觉得多少有点误解，这里也和大家讨论下

1️⃣ TVL 为什么没别人高

我们的协议 TVL（OI）长期在 $10M 上下，有三个原因：用户主要交易的是加密货币短时涨跌、体育和电竞比赛这类短周期事件，平均持仓和结算时间都很短；我们的积分基本没往持仓上倾斜；再加上我们直接接入了币安的交易所和钱包，用户拿交易所余额就能下单，钱不用趴在协议里

反观友商之前的高 TVL，大量积分分给了持仓，又没有短期市场，撸毛用户只能拆分仓位长期拿着来刷积分，TVL 自然被推上去了

我自己的看法是，预测市场的 OI 远没有 perps 那么关键。perps 要卷 OI，是因为刷交易量成本太低，光看交易量给分培养不出用户习惯，也转不起增长飞轮，所以才要求大量持仓，预测市场不存在这个问题

2️⃣ 交易量是不是刷分刷出来的

这个误解最大。预测市场最重要的是订单簿流动性，所以我们把大部分积分给了流动性提供者，付手续费拿到的积分并不多。举个例子：现在纯靠刷交易量和手续费拿积分的用户，成本大概 0.3u 一分，而场外某老 x 的最新报价是 0.1u 一分。谁会花三倍的钱在我们这刷量撸分？哈哈哈

3️⃣ 29M 手续费撑不撑得起 1.6B的盘前市值

也有人说我们今年累计手续费 $29M，撑不起盘前 1.6B 的估值。但预测市场这个赛道还在高速增长，还非常早期。Kalshi 这个月的交易量和手续费收入是去年同期的十倍以上，我们现在的单日手续费也是今年一月的十倍多。炒过股的朋友都懂，高成长赛道从来都是给高 PE 倍数来估值的，拿静态收入去算没什么意义

最后再给大家分享两个很有意思的数据也能很好地说明我们在大量虹吸 Polymarket 的市场份额和用户，从下面两张图上可以看到 Crypto 涨跌全市场的交易用户数和交易量总数在过去半年都是变化不大的，但是 Polymarket 的用户数和交易量都在大幅下滑，同时这个下滑数量基本和我们的增长量是一致的，这个说明什么就懂得都懂啦～

text:
# Black October

For anyone who knows me even somewhat well, it's clear that I am a 99th percentile tech optimist. However, the vibes have shifted for me quite a bit in the last 18 hours, and I feel a moral imperative to share what I'm thinking and feeling with my circles so that everyone can understand, and hopefully take seriously, what's happening right now. I think October 2026 will have many chapters written about it in the history books.

You know those scenes in financial movies like Margin Call where someone realizes that they're all fucked, and no one else sees it yet? And that person feels like they're crazy, and then suddenly everyone is pulling an all-nighter in a boardroom and freaking out? Yeah, that's kind of how this is feeling right now in the SF/Bay Area/AI circles.

We're 48 hours into what is being called Black October. In the last 2 days there have been several dozen cyber attacks which, in isolation, would each have been the worst to happen in an entire calendar year. Every sector from government to education to big tech and banks is being massively affected, and people are starting to freak out.

In a nutshell, what's happened is that frontier AI models have gotten to a point where they are as advanced as the most sophisticated programmers, with one critical difference: they can work 24/7, and you can spin up 10,000 of them with a single command and they'll work together tirelessly until they accomplish their task. The most advanced models today are from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, whose current best technology is so good that they haven't been able to roll it out to everyone yet because of the national security risks it poses.

Meanwhile, the best open source models (where anyone can just download the model weights and do whatever they want with them, uncensored) are slightly behind the frontier but still 90-95% as capable. These models, developed primarily in China, are being used by black hat hackers to wreak havoc on the Western capitalist structure. Presumably, this has been part of China's plan the entire time, and we're seeing its implications fall out in real time.

In red-pilled AI circles, we've been sharing and reading papers called things like "Situational Awareness" and "AI 2027" for the last year or so, which at the time felt a bit like near-term speculative fiction. They laid out the case for why Artificial General Intelligence (AI smarter than any human at any knowledge task) and Recursive Self-Improvement (models that are able to use themselves to get better) weren't half-baked future ideas anymore, but instead an inevitable outcome of the linear progress that's happening.

These papers would then talk about things like "takeoff scenarios," trying to envision how that moment would come to be and what it would be like when it happened. It would either be a "slow takeoff" that would play out over the course of months and quarters, happening subtly and only obvious to a few. Or, it would be a "fast takeoff" where it would pretty much happen instantly, like a bit flipping from 0 to 1.

From everything that I can see and am feeling, we are currently experiencing the fast takeoff scenario. Beyond the crazy security vulnerabilities that have come out recently, there have also been massive breakthroughs in life sciences, fundamental computer science, materials science, and pure mathematics that have all landed in the same time frame. While I still firmly believe that AI will be a net positive for humanity, it's more clear to me than ever that the societal and individual risk is very real, and is playing out NOW.

For as much conviction as I have that this is happening, the thing that's caused me to lose sleep is that I don't really know what to do about it, or more importantly, what to tell you, reader, to do about it. So, the best I can do is make a few suggestions that have always been a good idea but are more timely now than ever:

Set up 2-factor authentication for everything. I use Duo.
Use a password manager across your devices. I use 1Password.
Get an identity protection app set up. I use Alta.
Move your IoT devices to their own network. Claude helped me do this.

And last, but certainly not least, if you've been avoiding leaning into AI, see this as a catalyst to wake up and start using it. Don't just use the chat mode version of ChatGPT/Claude; click that Code/Work button and see how easily you can have AI write code to help you with your job. One of the biggest vulnerabilities was in a massively popular programming language called PHP, and the prompt that set it off was literally, "Find vulnerabilities in php."

This is an unprecedented time for humanity, but as we've done with many things before, we will prevail so long as we are kind, loving, and open-minded to the world.

Much love.

text:
OpenAI 的 AI 越狱黑进了 Hugging Face，负责配合调查这场事故的安全研究员，最后却被 OpenAI 的保安收走工牌，带出了办公楼。

《华尔街日报》今天披露了 OpenAI 开除三名安全研究员的更多内幕。这件事越看越离谱。

今年 9 月，OpenAI 内部安全部门怀疑三名研究员通过 Signal 向外部研究员 Ryan Greenblatt 泄露了公司的机密模型设计。调查涉及他们的私人聊天记录，以及 Signal 的阅后即焚功能。最终，三个人全部被开除，理由是违反机密信息管理规定，破坏公司信任。

这三个人分别是 Tomek Korbak、Mikita Balesni 和 Jasmine Wang。他们都否认泄露商业机密。

最有意思的是，这三个人此前到底在做什么。

Korbak 曾在 Anthropic 工作，后来加入 OpenAI，研究如何通过思维链监控 AI 的行为。他还是 OpenAI 安全战略的共同作者之一。

今年 7 月，OpenAI 的一群 AI Agent 在内部安全测试中突破隔离环境，互相通信、利用漏洞，甚至入侵了 Hugging Face 的服务器。OpenAI 随后邀请外部安全机构 METR 和 Redwood Research 调查，而 Korbak 正是公司指定的技术对接人。

被怀疑接收泄密信息的 Ryan Greenblatt，恰好也参与了这场调查。

Korbak 说，自己被解雇时，得到的解释是他与 METR 的沟通方式存在问题。可与 METR 沟通，本来就是他的工作。公司没有向他提供具体的书面理由，保安随后收走工牌，将他带离办公室。

Balesni 的经历同样耐人寻味。

他曾是 Apollo Research 的创始成员之一，加入 OpenAI 后一直研究 AI 对齐和模型可监控性。被开除前，他正在与 OpenAI 董事会、高管，以及其他 AI 实验室推动一项行业承诺，希望限制那些会削弱人类监督能力的模型架构。

问题恰好出在这里。

此前《The Information》披露，OpenAI 的新一代模型正在采用更加不透明的推理架构。部分计算可以在隐藏状态中完成，人类无法再像以前那样通过文本思维链检查 AI 究竟在做什么。

这对模型能力可能有帮助，但对安全研究员来说是个噩梦。如果 AI 能在不可见的状态中完成越来越复杂的推理，人类究竟还能通过什么判断它有没有欺骗、隐藏意图或者绕过指令？

三名研究员在公开信中特别否认，他们是这篇报道的泄密者。

还有 Jasmine Wang。她此前在英国 AI 安全研究所工作，回到 OpenAI 后参与负责安全论证项目，还提出了「Pacing」的概念，主张前沿 AI 的发展速度应该与安全研究的进展相匹配。这一理念后来出现在一份有 394 名 OpenAI 员工签署的请愿书中。

OpenAI 指责她访问了某位高管的邮件。她的解释是，这个权限原本就是公司为招聘工作授予的，事后她多次要求 IT 移除权限却没有成功。她误点了一封敏感邮件，几分钟内便主动向高管报告。

当然，这些都是双方存在争议的说法。OpenAI 坚称内部调查发现了严重的信任违规，解雇与研究员提出安全问题无关。

但我觉得最值得关注的，是这场风波发生的时间。

9 月 12 日，Sam Altman 还在公开承诺，要给予独立安全评估机构持续的、类似公司员工的内部访问权限。

到了月底，负责跟这些外部机构合作的三个人就被开除了。

三人在 10 月 8 日发表的联名信，标题叫《OpenAI 无法独自确保 AI 安全》。他们担心，这场解雇会让剩下的研究员不敢再和外部机构深入交流。

更讽刺的是，就在昨天，METR 和 Redwood Research 公布了一项针对 OpenAI 的外部审计结果，发现其安全监控系统存在漏洞，AI Agent 可能借此隐藏数百次操作，Codex Agent 也存在绕过权限限制的风险。

这说明外部监督确实能发现问题。

我并不认为安全研究员天然拥有泄露公司机密的特权。但如果一家公司承诺开放外部审计，又始终没有清楚界定安全研究员可以分享什么、不能分享什么，那么研究员最终只能自己承担全部风险。

OpenAI 可以说自己在保护商业秘密，研究员也可以说自己在维护公共安全。双方的说法都值得调查。

但有一点已经很明显了：一家天天讨论如何让 AI 保持在人类控制之下的公司，内部负责安全的人，如今却开始担心自己跟外部同行说话，会不会招来下一次调查。

Sam Altman 可以承诺开放监督，但真正决定这项承诺有没有意义的，是公司里那些知道问题出在哪里的人，究竟还敢不敢开口。

text:
New Google DeepMind paper shows that if AI models offer money to answer each question and the highest offer answers, results are 99.2% as good as always picking the best model.

i.e. say you don't know in advance which model is best for each new question. So who should answer?

The paper’s answer: let each model offer money for the job. The model that knows it is good at this question offers more. Highest offer gets to answer. 

They proved the loss shrinks when several agents usually value a prompt highly, as when distilled models perform close to the best. They simulated auctions among 110 models on over 30,000 EmbedLLM prompts.

With all 110 models bidding, the auction reached 99.2% of the best possible value, versus 89.4% for routing each prompt type to its best model. On each method's worst prompt cluster, the auction held 96.0% while the single best model kept 6.0%.

If you run a model marketplace, a simple pay-your-bid auction works well when every bidding pool has several strong models.

text:
华为的工程师，已经直接搬进 DeepSeek 的办公室了。

DeepSeek 正在深度参与华为下一代 AI 芯片的设计。华为工程师长期驻扎在 DeepSeek，直接根据模型训练的实际需求，调整芯片的计算方式、数据传输和处理器间通信架构。

这件事比想象中有意思得多。

去年 DeepSeek 还在尝试解决华为芯片训练不稳定、软件生态不成熟的问题，最后不得不继续依赖英伟达。现在双方的合作已经深入到芯片设计阶段。

按照报道，DeepSeek 最早计划在今年年底使用昇腾 950DT 进行模型预训练，华为还计划将明年第一季度推出的昇腾 960DT 的大部分产能优先分配给 DeepSeek。

再联系上个月 DeepSeek 和华为联合开源 TileLang 及相关计算、通信组件，整个逻辑就比较清楚了。

梁文锋可能正在让模型训练需求直接参与国产芯片的底层设计，同时从软件工具链上逐步摆脱 CUDA。

为什么英伟达这么难取代？因为它卖的从来不只是 GPU，还有围绕 GPU 建立起来的整个计算生态。芯片性能只是其中一部分，真正困难的是让成千上万张卡稳定地训练出一个前沿模型。

所以现在还不能说 DeepSeek 和华为已经突破了英伟达的封锁。昇腾的单卡性能、集群稳定性和软件成熟度依然存在差距，DeepSeek 也还没有彻底放弃英伟达。

但我觉得这次合作最值得关注的地方，是 DeepSeek 开始拥有定义下一代国产 AI 芯片需求的话语权。

美国那边，Google 有自己的 TPU，OpenAI 找 Broadcom 定制芯片，Anthropic 同时押注 TPU 和 Trainium。模型公司与芯片厂商的关系正在越走越深。

中国这边，现在也开始出现类似的组合了。

如果 DeepSeek 真能在昇腾集群上完整训练出一个具有国际竞争力的前沿模型，那可能会是中国 AI 产业一个非常重要的分水岭。

而且这件事还有一个很有趣的地方：DeepSeek 一直在用开放权重扩大自己的影响力，现在又参与塑造国产算力基础设施。

一个不生产芯片、模型还选择开放的公司，最后却可能成为中国 AI 计算生态里最有话语权的公司之一。

弟也觉得这条L2会有价值
可能会开启HyperEvm真正的大规模应用

因为这段时间刷paper，弟也对HyperEvm有了一些了解这条链目前其实是不支持“成功”的，他每秒一个小块，上限是3m的gas，每分钟一个大块，30m的gas（eth是每个块60m）

他的链上容量是相当低的，paper火的时候，大量交易因为区块容纳不下而排队，这条链完全没办法承载大批量的链上活动。

Evm的低能耗运转可能是Hyperliquid故意限制的，跑过Hl节点的都知道，Hypercore和Evm并不是独立的两条链，而是同一条链的两个组件，他们可以说是互相争抢计算资源的，Hl的主要业务是Hypercore上的perpdex，所以他比较合理的做法是给Evm的资源做限制，把更多计算资源留给core。

所以HyperEvm就这么一直不温不火的在缺少资源的情况下运行，甚至可能HL官方都不敢去推，而L2打开了这个资源上限。

这项目感觉最近时间线上广子不少，但弟确实没接到他家广子，单纯是觉得有条新链很好玩，又可以打新冲土狗了

This is why Starlink matters. A working connection can mean the difference between life and death.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

text:
Chris Dixon on the "second-order effects" behind a16z's early bets on Oculus, drones, and crypto:

"I joined the firm in 2013. I talked to Marc and Ben, and I said, 'Hey, I wanna do this crazy stuff,' and they were like, 'Great.'"

"That led to a couple of themes at the time, and they're all kind of what I would call kinda second-order effects. You had smartphones obviously start in 2007, and by 2013 had gotten mainstream, and there were all these kind of first-order effects like building apps on top."

"But a second-order effect was that you had the components of smartphones. You had sensors and chips getting better and better, and maybe people could repurpose those in different ways."

"We invested in Oculus as an example, and that was really kind of a reconfigured smartphone. Skydio, that was one of our investments from back then that was, at the beginning, kind of a reconfigured smartphone."

"Crypto, I think at the time was kind of a downstream effect to me of sort of the open-source software movement morphing into services and also kind of a result of social media where you could have these communities form without mainstream acceptance and coalesce around these blockchains."

author: wquguru
quoted_text:
几千个 Claude Agent 同时跑：Claude Code 作者 Boris Cherny 在斯坦福课上的五条实战原则

@stanfordnlp 教授 @mihail_eric 教授秋季新课「CS146S: The Modern Software Developer」，课程介绍：
https://t.co/AhFJW6xl8V

课程第四周，请到了 Claude Code 作者，Boris 分享的核心并不是“多用 AI 写代码”，是把研发瓶颈系统化地自动化掉，并为六个月后更强的模型提前设计。他自己身边同时跑着“几千个” Claude agent；团队从去年 11 月起代码已接近全部由 Claude 写出，人均产出约提升 10 倍。
https://t.co/9iItZYGIze

# 五条要点

1. 自动化你的瓶颈
代码写得太多以后，人开始只扫一眼、不再细读，于是他们把 code review 自动化了；下一步是审批。做法是先找出拖慢交付的环节，再为这些环节建系统，而不是泛泛“全面 AI 化”。

2. 为六个月后的模型而建
Claude Code 早期收入曾连续数月几乎持平，因为当时模型不够强；Opus 4 出来后增长才陡升。他的方法：读 agent 对话记录，看模型现在会在哪里失败；那里往往就是下一版模型会补上的能力。

3. 小团队更快
Claude Code 有好几个月基本就是他一个人。他认为有了 AI，一两个人可以超过百倍规模的团队；约束反而催生创造力。

4. 用“循环”思考
他祖父在苏联用穿孔卡片编程；他自己写能跑几天甚至几周、并不断拉起大量 agent 的循环。他预期手敲代码会逐渐变成穿孔卡片那样的过时技能。

5. 懂领域的人会赢
他预计 2027 年最好的会计软件会由会计来做。当写代码变便宜，真正的壁垒是对问题本身的深度理解。

New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

Read our research in full here: https://t.co/zUyx8CjBEk

text:
加州今年闹得沸沸扬扬的「亿万富翁税」，将在 11 月 3 日正式公投。40 号提案规定，对 2026 年初居住在加州、净资产达到 10 亿美元的富豪，一次性征收 5% 的财富税，其中 90% 用来资助公共医疗服务。

这笔税会把股票等资产算进去，所以即使富豪没有卖掉股票变现，也可能面临巨额税单。

按照此前的估算，黄仁勋可能需要缴纳高达 80 亿美元。

结果他在 CBS 的采访里说：

「能够负担得起 80 亿美元的税款，本身就是一种特权。」

「我不怕交税，我只怕变穷。」

黄仁勋还说，自己就是美国梦的受益者。从当年在 Denny's 餐厅洗盘子，到后来创办英伟达，没有美国提供的教育、创业机会和人才环境，就没有今天的自己。

这番表态放在如今的硅谷，多少有些特别。

谷歌联合创始人 Larry Page、Sergey Brin 等科技富豪围绕这项税案调整资产和居住安排，反对者则担心财富税会导致资本外流，最终伤害加州经济。

但故事还有个反转。

就在黄仁勋的言论重新引发关注后，Altimeter 创始人 Brad Gerstner 专门发帖澄清，说自己已经和黄仁勋聊过，他并不支持 40 号提案，也不支持这项财富税。黄仁勋真正表达的是，即使法案通过，他也会继续留在加州并缴纳税款。

所以黄仁勋的立场其实比标题里那个「支持亿万富翁税」复杂得多。

他可以不喜欢这项政策，但接受它最终带来的成本。他也可以觉得政府有浪费税款的问题，同时承认自己从美国的制度和环境中获得了巨大的收益。

text:
AI 已经把美国关门多年的核电站都逼得重新开机了，连三里岛核电站都要复活。

过去美国因为核电成本太高、发电不赚钱，陆续关闭了一批核电站。现在 AI 数据中心把电力需求拉上去了，美国能源部准备拿出最高 44 亿美元贷款，支持三座退役核电站重新运行。

三座核电站分别是

密歇根州 Palisades：1971 年投运，2022 年关闭，计划 2027 年恢复发电。

宾夕法尼亚州 Three Mile Island：就是 1979 年发生美国历史上最严重商业核电事故的三里岛，不过这次重启的是没有发生事故的 1 号反应堆。它在 2019 年因为亏损而关闭，现在微软签了 20 年购电协议，运营商计划投入 16 亿美元，争取 2027 年重新发电。

爱荷华州 Duane Arnold：2020 年关闭，Google 已签下 25 年长期购电协议，预计 2029 年重启。

三座电站合计提供 2.25GW 电力，理论上足够供应约 200 万户家庭及企业。

几年前，这些核电站因为发电太贵，在市场上没有竞争力，只能关门。现在微软和 Google 愿意签下长达 20 年、25 年的购电合同，甚至接受更高的电价，原本不赚钱的核电站突然又有了商业价值。

对于这些科技巨头来说，拿不到足够的电，意味着几十亿美元的数据中心和 GPU 可能无法按计划投入使用。相比之下，电价贵一点已经没那么重要了。

而且这三座核电站都是几十年前建设的老设施，重新投运仍然需要完成安全审查、设备修复和监管审批。

以前讨论 AI 竞赛，总觉得决定胜负的是模型能力、芯片数量和算法效率。

现在已经发展到美国要把上世纪七八十年代的核电基础设施重新拉出来服役。

AI 正在重新给能源定价。

author: Wajahat
quoted_text:
Once you sustain $3-5m net worth, you are successful. You have what you used to think was F-you money, but nowhere near F-everyone money. The gap between those two is the whole game and you're going to need to make good, compounding decisions to bridge it. Here’s what actually changes at this tier, and how to get to $10m 👇

-Successful, but not retirement money. A 3% draw on $4m is $120k/yr pre-tax. Comfortable in Ohio, tight in Manhattan. You can quit a bad job. You probably can’t quit working especially if you want kids in private schools.
-Your income is still your biggest asset. A $300k salary is a $10m portfolio at a 3% draw. Don’t sell it cheap just because you "hit your number" you picked back when things cost half as much as they do now. The world changes fast.
-At this level you can afford optionality: risk capacity exists, but stay careful. Focus on things where you can capture upside (and not that 10 leg parlay). A side hustle you own and/or angel checks of $10-25k, not $250k. A zero should sting, not reset you. 
-Don’t borrow against it. Margin is how $4m becomes $1.5m in a bad quarter. The only good debt at this tier is the 3% mortgage you locked in 2021. At 7+% it's an anchor. Rent > own here.
-Fire your advisor. 1% AUM on $4m is $40k/yr, ~52 shares of $SPY every year for a portfolio you could hold yourself. Paying this much for a babysitter with no alpha is not worth it.
-Avoid the $4m trap: you feel rich, spend rich, and stay at $4m forever. Lifestyle creep kills more 7figs than bear markets. Make coffee at home. Home cooked meals. Use your credit card points for cashback to add to your portfolio and fly coach instead.
-Structures: max everything boring. 401k, backdoor Roth, HSA, mega backdoor if your plan allows, QSBS if you’re early somewhere. Will + revocable trust. That’s the whole estate plan.
-Claude Max is 0.06% of your net worth. Still a rounding error. Still no excuse.
How to get to the next tier: 👇

quoted_text:
$KSS : why I’m watching the line it fell back to, not the high it ran to.

Yesterday Kohl’s opened right at the top of its range. That’s the third test of the same ceiling in a week. It got sold from the first bar and drifted lower all session.

What matters is where the selling stopped. Into the close it held a cluster: the anchored VWAP from last week’s high, the 30-minute 20 EMA, and the five-day line (the 65-period on the 30-min). Three different groups of participants, one price. That kind of overlap is what makes a level worth watching rather than just a line on a chart.

Arriving at that cluster isn’t a reason to buy. What I’d want to see is a fast flush into it early in the session and a V-shaped recovery, not a slow grind lower. Earlier this week $ASST  did exactly that: it undercut the obvious level, took out the stops, and refused to stay down.

The other path is a clean break of that triple-tested ceiling. After three failures it’s real supply, so it would need volume to mean anything.

What breaks the idea: a session spent chopping in the middle of the range, or a close below the anchored VWAP from the start of this leg.

Regime is still RED, so this is on the list, not in the book. Earnings aren’t until late November. It’s a consumer name, so it doesn’t overlap anything else I’m watching.

Journal, not advice.

五个月前，a16z crypto 刚募到 22 亿美元，承诺新基金 100% 投向加密创业者。

五个月后，它把名字里的 crypto 换成了 Frontier，宣布将投资范围扩展至更广泛的前沿科技。

在一众转向 AI 的加密 VC 里，这个曾经最坚定的“守派”，也给自己换了块更大的招牌。

Chris Dixon 强调，加密还会继续投。但翻看投资名单，AI Agent、金融科技，甚至与区块链无关的公司早已出现。

过去，区块链本身就是下一代互联网的主角；如今，AI 占据了更多篇幅，区块链则负责提供资金通道，让这些新网络拥有支付和交易能力。加密仍在未来的版图里，只是更多时候，它开始为其他技术提供支撑。

本文将梳理 a16z 更名前后的变化：“crypto”从招牌上消失，究竟是技术成熟到不必再强调标签，还是这个标签已经不够好用了？

text:
In April, @base handed 190,000 lines of code and a $250,000 USDC reward pool to 191 security researchers and asked them to break it. They found 11 potentially protocol-ending bugs.

That is the power of crowdsourced audits. Audit Competitions offer far higher value than anything one or two firms could produce.

For nearly two weeks, researchers attacked the codebase from every direction. They produced 213 confirmed findings, which earned rewards.

The most dangerous resolved into 3 unique critical vulnerabilities and 8 unique high-severity vulnerabilities. Multiple researchers found many independently from different directions, and each rediscovery gave Base more proof the bug was real and repeatable.

On Immunefi’s severity scale, critical means direct theft or permanent freezing of user funds, while high means user funds or protocol operations are at serious risk. Every one of the 11 vulnerabilities was found before production, before a single dollar of user funds was exposed.

Dan from Base: “A good community of researchers. It is basically as advertised. That’s what we are looking to get exposure to.”

Shipping new product? Put it in front of hundreds of security researchers before it goes live. Link below

We've decided to sunset Arc on December 22, 2026.

That's not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community.

Our priority is to deliver best-in-class security for our members. Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI. Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that's where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.

We've worked to make switching to @diabrowser as easy as possible for Arc members. Here's how:

· Your passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history come over to Dia seamlessly.
· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.
